Surah Ghafir: eighty-five verses. Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿Ha, Mim.﴾ ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing,﴾ ﴿the Forgiver of sin, the Acceptor of repentance, Severe in punishment, the Possessor of bounty. There is no god but Him; to Him is the final return.﴾ ﴿None dispute the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve, so do not let their movement throughout the land deceive you.﴾ ﴿The people of Noah denied before them, and so did the factions after them. And every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him, and they argued with falsehood to refute the truth by it. So I seized them. Then how was My punishment?﴾ ﴿Thus the word of your Lord has been fulfilled against those who disbelieved: that they are the companions of the Fire.﴾ ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with His praise and believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who believe: "Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire.﴾ [Ghafir: 7] ﴿Our Lord, admit them to the Gardens of Eden which You promised them, along with whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring. Indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ [Ghafir: 8] ﴿And protect them from evil deeds. Whoever You protect from evil deeds on that Day, You have truly shown them mercy. That is the great triumph.﴾ [Ghafir: 9] ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve will be called out: "The aversion of Allah towards you is greater than your aversion towards yourselves, when you were called to faith and you disbelieved."﴾ [Ghafir: 10] ﴿They will say: "Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and gave us life twice. So we have acknowledged our sins; is there any way out?"﴾ [Ghafir: 11] ﴿That is because when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved; but when partners were associated with Him, you believed. So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Great.﴾ [Ghafir: 12] ﴿It is He who shows you His signs and sends down provision for you from the sky. But none remember except those who turn back (to Allah).﴾ [Ghafir: 13] ﴿So invoke Allah, making your religion sincerely His, even though the disbelievers dislike it.﴾ [Ghafir: 14] ﴿Lofty in rank, Lord of the Throne, He casts the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants, to warn of the Day of Meeting.﴾ [Ghafir: 15] ﴿The Day when they will come forth, and nothing about them will be hidden from Allah. "Whose is the kingdom today?" "It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer."﴾ [Ghafir: 16] ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. There is no injustice today. Indeed Allah is swift in reckoning.﴾ [Ghafir: 17] ﴿And warn them of the Approaching Day, when hearts will be at the throats, choking with grief. The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend nor any intercessor who will be obeyed.﴾ [Ghafir: 18] ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the chests conceal.﴾ [Ghafir: 19] ﴿And Allah judges with truth, while those they invoke besides Him do not judge anything. Indeed Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾ [Ghafir: 20] ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and in traces left upon the earth, yet Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no protector against Allah.﴾ [Ghafir: 21] ﴿That is because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed He is Strong, Severe in punishment.﴾ [Ghafir: 22] ﴿And We sent Moses with Our signs and clear authority﴾ [Ghafir: 23] ﴿to Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun. They said: "A sorcerer, a liar."﴾ [Ghafir: 24] ﴿When he brought them the truth from Us, they said: "Kill the sons of those who believe with him, and spare their women." But the plotting of the disbelievers is only in error.﴾ [Ghafir: 25] ﴿Pharaoh said: "Leave me to kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed I fear that he will change your religion or that he will cause corruption in the land."﴾ [Ghafir: 26] ﴿Moses said: "I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning."﴾ [Ghafir: 27] ﴿A believing man from Pharaoh's family, who was concealing his faith, said: "Will you kill a man because he says, 'My Lord is Allah,' and he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? If he is a liar, his lie will fall upon him; but if he is truthful, some of what he threatens you with will befall you. Indeed Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar.﴾ [Ghafir: 28] ﴿O my people, yours is the kingdom today, dominant in the land. But who will help us against the might of Allah if it comes upon us?" Pharaoh said: "I only show you what I see, and I guide you only to the path of right conduct."﴾ [Ghafir: 29] ﴿And the one who believed said: "O my people, I fear for you a day like the day of the factions﴾ [Ghafir: 30] ﴿like the custom of the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, and those after them. And Allah does not desire injustice for His servants.﴾ [Ghafir: 31] ﴿O my people, I fear for you the Day of Calling Out﴾ [Ghafir: 32] ﴿the day you will turn your backs fleeing. You will have no protector from Allah, and whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide.﴾ [Ghafir: 33] ﴿Yusuf had already brought you clear proofs before, but you remained in doubt about what he brought you. Then when he died, you said: "Allah will never send a messenger after him." Thus Allah leaves astray whoever is a transgressor and a doubter.﴾ [Ghafir: 34] (p. 445) ﴿Those who dispute the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them, it is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah and of those who believe. Thus Allah seals every heart of an arrogant, tyrannical person.﴾ [Ghafir: 35] ﴿And Pharaoh said: "O Haman, build for me a tower that I may reach the ways﴾ [Ghafir: 36] ﴿the ways to the heavens, and look upon the God of Moses. Indeed I think he is a liar." Thus the evil of his deeds was made attractive to Pharaoh, and he was barred from the way. And the plotting of Pharaoh was nothing but ruin.﴾ [Ghafir: 37] ﴿And the one who believed said: "O my people, follow me, and I will guide you to the path of right conduct.﴾ [Ghafir: 38] ﴿O my people, this worldly life is only a passing enjoyment, and indeed the Hereafter is the abode of permanence.﴾ [Ghafir: 39] ﴿Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its equivalent, and whoever does righteousness, male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise, being provided therein without account.﴾ [Ghafir: 40] ﴿O my people, what is wrong with me that I invite you to salvation while you invite me to the Fire?﴾ [Ghafir: 41] ﴿You invite me to disbelieve in Allah and to associate with Him what I have no knowledge of, while I invite you to the Mighty, the Forgiving.﴾ [Ghafir: 42] ﴿Undoubtedly, what you invite me to has no call in this world or in the Hereafter, and our return is to Allah, and the transgressors are the companions of the Fire.﴾ [Ghafir: 43] ﴿So you will remember what I say to you. I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed Allah is All-Seeing of the servants.﴾ [Ghafir: 44] ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted, and the terrible punishment encompassed the family of Pharaoh.﴾ [Ghafir: 45] ﴿The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening; and on the Day the Hour is established: "Admit the family of Pharaoh to the severest punishment."﴾ [Ghafir: 46] ﴿And when they argue in the Fire, the weak will say to those who were arrogant: "Indeed we were following you, so will you relieve us of a portion of the Fire?"﴾ [Ghafir: 47] ﴿Those who were arrogant will say: "Indeed we are all in it. Indeed Allah has judged between the servants."﴾ [Ghafir: 48] ﴿And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell: "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of punishment."﴾ [Ghafir: 49] ﴿They will say: "Did your messengers not come to you with clear proofs?" They will say: "Yes." They will say: "Then call upon them." But the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error.﴾ [Ghafir: 50] ﴿Indeed We will help Our messengers and those who believed in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir: 51] ﴿the Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers. For them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode.﴾ [Ghafir: 52] ﴿And We gave Moses guidance, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book﴾ [Ghafir: 53] ﴿as guidance and a reminder for people of understanding.﴾ [Ghafir: 54] ﴿So be patient; indeed the promise of Allah is true. And ask forgiveness for your sin, and glorify your Lord with praise in the evening and the morning.﴾ [Ghafir: 55] ﴿Indeed those who dispute the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them, there is nothing in their chests but pride, which they will never attain. So seek refuge in Allah; indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾ [Ghafir: 56] ﴿Surely the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most people do not know.﴾ [Ghafir: 57] ﴿The blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer. Little do you remember.﴾ [Ghafir: 58] ﴿Indeed the Hour is coming, there is no doubt in it, but most people do not believe.﴾ [Ghafir: 59] ﴿And your Lord says: "Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Indeed those who are too arrogant to worship Me will enter Hell, humiliated."﴾ [Ghafir: 60] ﴿It is Allah who made the night for you that you may rest in it, and the day giving sight. Indeed Allah is full of bounty toward mankind, but most people do not give thanks.﴾ [Ghafir: 61] ﴿That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things. There is no god but Him. So how are you turned away?﴾ [Ghafir: 62] ﴿Thus are turned away those who used to deny the signs of Allah.﴾ [Ghafir: 63] ﴿It is Allah who made the earth a resting place for you and the sky a canopy, and shaped you and perfected your forms, and provided you with good things. That is Allah, your Lord. So blessed is Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [Ghafir: 64] ﴿He is the Living; there is no god but Him. So invoke Him, making your religion sincerely His. Praise belongs to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [Ghafir: 65] ﴿Say: "Indeed I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides Allah, since clear proofs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds."﴾ [Ghafir: 66] ﴿It is He who created you from dust, then from a drop, then from a clinging clot, then brings you out as a child, then that you may reach your maturity, then that you may become elders, though some of you are taken before that, and that you may reach a specified term, and that perhaps you will reason.﴾ [Ghafir: 67] ﴿It is He who gives life and causes death. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ [Ghafir: 68] ﴿Have you not seen those who dispute the signs of Allah? How are they turned away?﴾ [Ghafir: 69] ﴿Those who denied the Book and what We sent with Our messengers; they will soon know﴾ [Ghafir: 70] ﴿when the shackles and chains are around their necks, and they are dragged﴾ [Ghafir: 71] ﴿in the scalding water, then in the Fire they are burned.﴾ [Ghafir: 72]

Azifa al-shay': it drew near. The poet said:
"The time of departure has drawn near, but our mounts have not yet moved from our saddles, and it is as if it had already come."

Al-tabab: ruin. Al-silsila: the chain, which is well known. Al-sahb: dragging. Sajjara al-tannur: I filled the oven with fire.

Ha, Mim. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing; the Forgiver of sin, the Acceptor of repentance, severe in punishment, the Possessor of bounty; there is no god but Him; to Him is the final return. None dispute the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve, so do not let their movement throughout the land deceive you. The people of Noah denied before them, and so did the factions after them; and every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him, and they argued with falsehood to refute the truth by it, so I seized them, and how was My punishment? Thus the word of your Lord has been fulfilled against those who disbelieved: that they are the companions of the Fire.

The Hawamim (the seven surahs beginning with Ha-Mim) are all Meccan, according to unanimous agreement. It has been said that some verses of these surahs are Medinan, but Ibn 'Atiyya said: this is weak.

It is related in a hadith: "The Hawamim are the brocade of the Qur'an." And in it: "Whoever wishes to graze in the pleasant gardens of Paradise, let him recite the Hawamim." And in it: "The likeness of the Hawamim in the Qur'an is like the likeness of the striped patterns in garments."

These Hawamim are devoted to admonition, warning, and the paths of the Hereafter, and they are short, so weariness does not affect them.

The connection of the beginning of this surah to the end of al-Zumar is that when He, the Exalted, mentioned the final state of the disbelievers and the believers, He mentioned here "the Forgiver of sin and the Acceptor of repentance," so that this would be an invitation for the disbeliever to faith, and to giving up what he is engaged in, and to show that the door of repentance is open. He mentioned the severity of His punishment, and that the whole world will be subject to it, so that one would refrain from what he is engaged in, and that his return is to his Lord, who will recompense him for what he does of good or evil.

It is read with a fatha on the ha' (Ha, with the vowel fatha), chosen by Abu al-Qasim ibn Jubara al-Hudhali, author of the book al-Kamil fi al-Qur'an. Abu al-Sammal read it with a kasra, on the basis of the meeting of two unvocalized consonants. Ibn Abi Ishaq and 'Isa read it with a fatha. It has been explained that the fatha is the vowel of meeting of two unvocalized consonants, and that it was a fatha for the sake of lightness, as in "ayna." Or it is an inflectional vowel, governed by an implied verb whose estimated form is: "Recite Ha Mim."

It is related in a hadith that a Bedouin asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about "Ha Mim," what is it? He said: "They are names and openings of surahs." Shurayh ibn Abi Awfa al-Absi said:
"Ha Mim reminds me, while the spear is shaking, so why did he not recite Ha Mim before the advance?"

Al-Kumayt said:
"We found among you, in the family of Hamim, a sign, which a pious and eloquent one interpreted for us."

They inflected "Hamim" and it was not declined (not given tanwin) because of being a proper noun, or because of being a proper noun together with a resemblance to foreign origin, since fa'il is not among the patterns of Arabic word forms, and this is found only in foreign words, like Qabil and Habil.

It has been mentioned in the hadith that "Ha Mim" is pluralized as "Hawamim," just as "Ta Sin" [al-Naml: 1] is pluralized as "Tawasin."

Abu Hayyan's commentary on surah 40, verses 1–6 (part 2 of 3):

Ṣāḥib Zād al-Masīr related on the authority of his teacher Ibn Manṣūr, the linguist, that he said: "It is an error to say, 'I recited the Ḥawāmīm' (al-Ḥawāmīm), for it is not from the speech of the Arabs; the correct form is to say, 'I recited Āl Ḥā Mīm.'" And in a ḥadīth of Ibn Mas'ūd: "If you come upon Āl Ḥamīm, you have come upon meadows, soft and fragrant." End of quotation.

If it is established that the Messenger (ﷺ) actually said, "al-Ḥawāmīm," it would be a proof against those who forbid it. But if it was transmitted by meaning, it is possible that it is a distortion by non-Arabs.

Do you not see Ibn Mas'ūd's wording, "If you come upon Āl Ḥamīm," and the verse of al-Kumayt: "We found for you in Āl Ḥāmīm"? The discussion of these disjoined letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭa'ah) has already passed at the beginning of al-Baqarah. Some have added other opinions concerning Ḥā Mīm here, which are transmitted from the early generations (al-salaf). We have dispensed with mentioning them, because they are confused and there is no evidence for the soundness of any of them.

If Ḥā Mīm is the name of the surah, it occupies a position of nominative (raf') as a subject (mubtadaʾ), and "Tanzīl" is then its predicate with "min Allāh" as the predicate. Otherwise, "Tanzīl" is a subject and "min Allāh" is the predicate; or it is the predicate of an implied subject, i.e., "this is the tanzīl," and "min Allāh" is related to "tanzīl."

﴿al-ʿAzīz al-ʿAlīm﴾: two attributes indicating intensity in power, dominance, and knowledge, and they are among the attributes of the Essence (ṣifāt al-dhāt).

Al-Zajjāj said: "Ghāfir" and "Qābil" are attributes, and "Shadīd" is an apposition (badal). End of quotation.

He made "Ghāfir" and "Qābil" attributes even though they are active participles (ismā fāʿil), because it is understood from them that they are not intended to denote renewal or restriction to a time, but rather continuity and permanence. Their annexation (iḍāfah) is genuine (maḥḍah), so they are definite, and it is correct for a definite noun to be described by them. "Shadīd al-ʿiqāb" is parsed as an apposition because it belongs to the category of the attributive adjective (al-ṣifah al-mushabbahah), which does not become definite through annexation to a definite noun. Sībawayh has explicitly stated that any noun whose annexation is not genuine, when annexed to a definite noun, may be intended as genuine annexation, and thus becomes definite and can describe a definite noun, except for what belongs to the category of the attributive adjective, which does not become definite.

The author of al-Muqniʿ relates from the Kufans that they permitted, in "ḥusn al-wajh" and similar expressions, that it be an attribute of a definite noun. He said: "That is an error according to the Basrans, because ḥusn al-wajh is indefinite, and when you want to define it, you add al-." 

Abu al-Ḥajjāj al-Aʿlam said: "It is not far-fetched that ḥusn al-wajh be intended as definite, since annexation does not prevent it." End of quotation. This is a leaning toward the Kufan position.

Some have made "Ghāfir al-dhanb" and what follows it appositions, considering that they do not become definite through annexation, as if he had regarded the future time in "Ghāfir" and "Qābil."

It has also been said: "Ghāfir" and "Qābil" are not intended to refer to the past; they become definite through annexation and are attributes, meaning that His decree of forgiveness and acceptance of repentance is in this world.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: Al-Zajjāj's making "Shadīd al-ʿiqāb" alone an apposition among the attributes contains a clear flaw. The proper view is to say: since a single indefinite noun is placed among these definite nouns, it indicates that all of them are appositions and not attributes. An example of this is a poem whose feet all come in the form of mustafʿilun; it is judged to be of the rajaz meter. If one foot in it comes as mutafāʿilun, it becomes of the kāmil meter, and there is no flaw in that, because following the established and sound rules is the original principle.

His statement, "it indicates that all of them are appositions," is itself a fault of composition not in Arabic, because he made "fa-qad ādhanat" the answer to "lammā," and it is not from their speech to say: "lammā qāma Zaydun fa-qad qāma ʿAmrun." His statement, "that all of them are appositions," involves repetition of appositions. As for an apposition of an apposition according to those who affirm it, appositions do repeat in it. As for apposition of whole from whole, partial apposition, and apposition of inclusion, I know of no statement from any grammarian permitting or forbidding repetition in them, except that in the words of one of our companions there is something indicating that an apposition is not repeated. That occurs in the verse of the poet:

Then to the son of Umm Unās I ride my she-camel,
ʿAmr, so that my she-camel reaches him or crawls to him.

A king, when the delegations alight at his gate,
they know the sources of his cloud, which do not run dry.

He said: "So 'malik' is an apposition of ʿAmr, an indefinite apposition of a definite noun." He said: "If you say, why is it not an apposition of Ibn Umm Unās? I say: because ʿAmr has already been made an apposition of it, so it is not permissible to make it an apposition again, since it has been dropped." End of quotation.

This indicates that an apposition is not repeated, and the appositive noun is one; and it indicates that an apposition of an apposition is permissible. His statement, "their feet come," is the plural of tif'āl, tif'ūl, tif'ūl, or tif'īl, and none of these patterns is a modified form at the end of the ʿarūḍ; rather its feet are limited, and none of them is among these patterns. So the correct statement would be: "its feet all come as mustafʿilun."

Sībawayh also said: "One may say they are attributes, and the alif and lam were omitted from 'Shadīd al-ʿiqāb' in order to match what precedes and follows it in sound. They have changed much of their speech from its rules for the sake of rhyme (izdiwāj), to the extent that they said: 'mā yaʿrifu suḥādilayhi min ʿanādilayhi,' so they made the dual of what is odd (witr) for the sake of what is even (shaf')." End of quotation.

Moreover, al-Khalīl said, regarding their saying: "It is not fitting for a man like you to do that, and it is fitting for a better man than you to do," that it is intended with the alif and lam, just as "al-jammāʾ al-ghafīr" is intended without the alif and lam. What facilitates this is the absence of confusion and the vagueness of the described noun. End of quotation.

There is no need to believe that the alif and lam were dropped from "Shadīd al-ʿiqāb," abandoning what is fundamental in grammar and likening it to a rare form deviating from the rules, namely the dual of the odd for the even. The Book of God is to be exalted above all of this.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: It may be said that he deliberately made it indefinite and vague, to indicate the extreme severity and that there is nothing more grievous than it, and to increase the warning. It may also be said that this nuance is what motivates choosing apposition over attribute when one follows the path of apposition. End of quotation.

Makkī permitted in "Ghāfir" and "Qābil" apposition, considering them indefinite because of their reference to the future, and attribute, considering them definite because of their reference to the past. Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Rāzī said: There is no dispute that "Ghāfir" and "Qābil" are attributes; they are so because they express the sense of permanence and continuity, and likewise "Shadīd al-ʿiqāb" conveys that, because His attributes are exempt from occurrence and renewal. Its meaning is: that His punishment is such that it is severe, and this meaning is always present; it is not described as having come about after it was not. End of quotation.

This is the statement of one who has not studied grammar or examined it, and it entails that "ḥakīm ʿalīm" in His saying "from the presence of One Wise, All-Knowing" (al-Naml: 6) and "malīk muqtadir" in His saying "in the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful" (al-Qamar: 55) are definite for the sake of exalting His attributes above occurrence and renewal, and because they are attributes that did not come about after they were not; and that the definition of attributes by al-, and their indefiniteness, would be equal. No beginner in grammar would go this way, let alone one who has written on it and presumed to interpret the Book of God.

From this lengthy discussion it emerges that "Ghāfir al-dhanb" and what is conjoined to it, and "Shadīd al-ʿiqāb," are attributes, because what is conjoined to an attribute is an attribute, and all of them are definite according to what has been established; or they are appositions, because what is conjoined to an apposition is an apposition, given that all of them are indefinite.

Or "Ghāfir" and "Qābil" are attributes, and "Shadīd" is an apposition to the definiteness of those two and the indefiniteness of "Shadīd."

Al-Zamakhsharī said: (If you ask): what is the role of the waw in His saying "wa-Qābil al-tawb"? (I answer): in it is a magnificent nuance, namely the gathering for the sinning repentant one of two mercies: that He accepts his repentance and records it for him as one of the acts of obedience, and that He makes it an erasure of sins, as if he had not sinned; as if He said: "Gatherer of forgiveness and acceptance." End of quotation.

How much this man reaches for and bursts into eloquence! What he has conveyed, that the waw is for gathering, is well known from the apparent principles of grammar.

The author of al-Ghunyān said: "It only conjoined them because they are associated and inseparable, one from the other. And 'Shadīd al-ʿiqāb' was cut off from them and not conjoined, because it stands alone." End of quotation. This is a Muʿtazilī inclination.

The doctrine of the People of the Sunnah is that God may forgive the disobedient, even if he does not repent, except for shirk. "Al-tawb" may be understood as a collective noun like "al-dhanb," or as the plural of tawbah, like bashr and bashrah, or sāʿin and sāʿah. The apparent meaning of His saying "wa-Qābil al-tawb" is that the repentance of the disobedient one, short of disbelief, is certainly accepted, just as the repentance of one who has disbelieved.

Regarding the certainty of accepting the repentance of the disobedient, the People of the Sunnah mention two views.

When God mentioned the severity of His punishment, He followed it with what gives hope in His mercy, namely His saying "Dhī al-Ṭawl," so this came as a threat flanked by two promises. Ibn ʿAbbās said: al-ṭawl is abundance and wealth; Qatādah said: blessings; Ibn Zayd said: power. His saying "ṭawlihi" means the multiplication of the good deeds of His friends and His pardon of their evil deeds.

When He mentioned a portion of His supreme attributes, essential and active, He mentioned that He alone is the Deity, and that to Him is the return on the Day of Assembly. Then He mentioned the state of those who dispute concerning the Book, and followed it with mention of the obedient among His angels and righteous servants, saying: ﴿None dispute concerning the signs of God except those who disbelieve﴾. Their disputing about them was saying at one time, "magic," at another, "poetry," at another, "tales of the ancients," and at another, "a human only teaches him." So it is disputation by falsehood, and He indicated this by His saying: ﴿and they disputed by falsehood to refute the truth thereby﴾.

Al-Suddī said: "yujādilu" means "yumārī" (contends). Ibn Salām said: "yajḥadu" (denies). Abū al-ʿĀliyah said: it was revealed concerning al-Ḥārith ibn Qays, one of the mockers.

As for what takes place among the people of knowledge regarding reflection upon them, clarifying their meanings, deriving rulings and beliefs from them, and contending with the people of innovation through them, there is abundant reward in that.

Then He forbade the listener to be deceived by the movement of these disbelievers in the lands and their dealings there, with what I have granted them of dwellings, farms, dominions, trade, and gains; and Quraysh used to trade in Syria and Yemen. For that is a burden upon them and a cause of their destruction, just as those before them who denied the messengers were destroyed.

The majority read ﴿fa-lā yaghrurka﴾ with unassimilated form (bi-l-fakk), and this is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz.

Zayd ibn ʿAlī and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read "fa-lā yaghurrak," with assimilation and a fatḥah on the rāʾ, and this is the dialect of Tamīm.

Since the disputation of the disbelievers arose from denying what the Messenger (peace be upon him) brought of the signs of God, He mentioned those among the earlier nations who denied before them, and what their condition came to of the descent of God's vengeance upon them, so that the disbelievers to whom the Messenger (peace be upon him) was sent might be deterred. So He began with the people of Noah, since he (peace be upon him) was the first messenger on earth, and He joined to his people "al-aḥzāb," who are those who banded together against the messengers and did not accept what they came with from God; among them were ʿĀd, Thamūd, Pharaoh and his followers.

He placed the intention to seize before disputation by falsehood, because when God protected the messengers from them so that they could not kill them, they returned to disputation by falsehood. The majority read ﴿bi-rasūlihim﴾ ("their messenger"); ʿAbd Allāh read "bi-rasūlihā" ("its messenger"), the pronoun referring to the wording "ummah" (community).

﴿li-yaʾkhudhūhu﴾: that they might gain control over him, by imprisonment, torture, or killing. Ibn ʿAbbās said: li-yaʾkhudhūhu means li-yamlikūhu (that they might possess him), and Quṭrub recited:

If you seize me and kill me, how many a seizer has desired my immortality!

It is said of the slain and the captive: "akhīdh." Qatādah said: li-yaʾkhudhūhu means li-yaqtulūhu (that they might kill him), expressing the effect by its cause.

﴿wa-jādalū bi-l-bāṭil﴾: i.e., by that which is vanishing and perishing, having no stability. It was also said: "al-bāṭil" is disbelief; it was said: it is Satan; it was said: by their saying: ﴿You are only human beings like us﴾ (Yā-Sīn: 15).

﴿li-yudḥiḍū bihi al-ḥaqq﴾: that they might cause the truth to slip away; i.e., the firm, true thing.

﴿fa-akhadhtuhum﴾: so I seized them, i.e., I destroyed them.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 40, verse 1–6 (part 3 of 3):

﴿Then how was My punishment﴾ — this is a rhetorical question (istifham ta'ajjub) expressing wonder at their annihilation and magnifying what befell them, not a question about the manner (kayfiyyah) of their punishment. They used to pass by their dwellings and see the traces of God's blessing upon them. He dispensed with the ya' of possession (ya' al-idafah), using the kasrah instead, because it falls at the end of a verse (fasilah); the original form is ʿiqābī.

﴿And thus was it decreed﴾ — i.e., just as that necessity of punishment was incumbent upon those [earlier peoples], so it was incumbent upon the disbelievers, by virtue of their being among the companions of the Fire, both those who came before them and those who came after.

(Annahum): it is a substitute (badal) for ﴿the word of your Lord﴾, so it is in the nominative position (fi mawdi' raf'). It is also permissible that the implied phrase is li-annahum, with the lam of causation (lam al-'illah) omitted. The meaning: just as the destruction of those nations was necessary, so the destruction of these people is necessary, because the cause that necessitates their destruction is a common attribute that unites them, namely their being among the companions of the Fire.

In the codex of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) it reads: "wa-kadhalika sabaqat" (and thus has preceded), which is an interpretation of meaning (tafsir ma'na), not a recitation (qira'ah). Ibn Hurmuz, Shaybah, Ibn al-Qa'qa', Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir recited ﴿kalimat﴾ in the plural; Abu Raja', Qatadah and the rest of the Seven recited it in the singular.

[p. 444]

Surah Ghafir: eighty-five verses. Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿Ha, Mim.﴾ ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing,﴾ ﴿the Forgiver of sin, the Acceptor of repentance, Severe in punishment, the Possessor of bounty. There is no god but Him; to Him is the final return.﴾ ﴿None dispute the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve, so do not let their movement throughout the land deceive you.﴾ ﴿The people of Noah denied before them, and so did the factions after them. And every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him, and they argued with falsehood to refute the truth by it. So I seized them. Then how was My punishment?﴾ ﴿Thus the word of your Lord has been fulfilled against those who disbelieved: that they are the companions of the Fire.﴾ ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with His praise and believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who believe: "Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire.﴾ [Ghafir: 7] ﴿Our Lord, admit them to the Gardens of Eden which You promised them, along with whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring. Indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ [Ghafir: 8] ﴿And protect them from evil deeds. Whoever You protect from evil deeds on that Day, You have truly shown them mercy. That is the great triumph.﴾ [Ghafir: 9] ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve will be called out: "The aversion of Allah towards you is greater than your aversion towards yourselves, when you were called to faith and you disbelieved."﴾ [Ghafir: 10] ﴿They will say: "Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and gave us life twice. So we have acknowledged our sins; is there any way out?"﴾ [Ghafir: 11] ﴿That is because when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved; but when partners were associated with Him, you believed. So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Great.﴾ [Ghafir: 12] ﴿It is He who shows you His signs and sends down provision for you from the sky. But none remember except those who turn back (to Allah).﴾ [Ghafir: 13] ﴿So invoke Allah, making your religion sincerely His, even though the disbelievers dislike it.﴾ [Ghafir: 14] ﴿Lofty in rank, Lord of the Throne, He casts the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants, to warn of the Day of Meeting.﴾ [Ghafir: 15] ﴿The Day when they will come forth, and nothing about them will be hidden from Allah. "Whose is the kingdom today?" "It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer."﴾ [Ghafir: 16] ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. There is no injustice today. Indeed Allah is swift in reckoning.﴾ [Ghafir: 17] ﴿And warn them of the Approaching Day, when hearts will be at the throats, choking with grief. The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend nor any intercessor who will be obeyed.﴾ [Ghafir: 18] ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the chests conceal.﴾ [Ghafir: 19] ﴿And Allah judges with truth, while those they invoke besides Him do not judge anything. Indeed Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾ [Ghafir: 20] ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and in traces left upon the earth, yet Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no protector against Allah.﴾ [Ghafir: 21] ﴿That is because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed He is Strong, Severe in punishment.﴾ [Ghafir: 22] ﴿And We sent Moses with Our signs and clear authority﴾ [Ghafir: 23] ﴿to Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun. They said: "A sorcerer, a liar."﴾ [Ghafir: 24] ﴿When he brought them the truth from Us, they said: "Kill the sons of those who believe with him, and spare their women." But the plotting of the disbelievers is only in error.﴾ [Ghafir: 25] ﴿Pharaoh said: "Leave me to kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed I fear that he will change your religion or that he will cause corruption in the land."﴾ [Ghafir: 26] ﴿Moses said: "I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning."﴾ [Ghafir: 27] ﴿A believing man from Pharaoh's family, who was concealing his faith, said: "Will you kill a man because he says, 'My Lord is Allah,' and he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? If he is a liar, his lie will fall upon him; but if he is truthful, some of what he threatens you with will befall you. Indeed Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar.﴾ [Ghafir: 28] ﴿O my people, yours is the kingdom today, dominant in the land. But who will help us against the might of Allah if it comes upon us?" Pharaoh said: "I only show you what I see, and I guide you only to the path of right conduct."﴾ [Ghafir: 29] ﴿And the one who believed said: "O my people, I fear for you a day like the day of the factions﴾ [Ghafir: 30] ﴿like the custom of the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, and those after them. And Allah does not desire injustice for His servants.﴾ [Ghafir: 31] ﴿O my people, I fear for you the Day of Calling Out﴾ [Ghafir: 32] ﴿the day you will turn your backs fleeing. You will have no protector from Allah, and whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide.﴾ [Ghafir: 33] ﴿Yusuf had already brought you clear proofs before, but you remained in doubt about what he brought you. Then when he died, you said: "Allah will never send a messenger after him." Thus Allah leaves astray whoever is a transgressor and a doubter.﴾ [Ghafir: 34] (p. 445) ﴿Those who dispute the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them, it is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah and of those who believe. Thus Allah seals every heart of an arrogant, tyrannical person.﴾ [Ghafir: 35] ﴿And Pharaoh said: "O Haman, build for me a tower that I may reach the ways﴾ [Ghafir: 36] ﴿the ways to the heavens, and look upon the God of Moses. Indeed I think he is a liar." Thus the evil of his deeds was made attractive to Pharaoh, and he was barred from the way. And the plotting of Pharaoh was nothing but ruin.﴾ [Ghafir: 37] ﴿And the one who believed said: "O my people, follow me, and I will guide you to the path of right conduct.﴾ [Ghafir: 38] ﴿O my people, this worldly life is only a passing enjoyment, and indeed the Hereafter is the abode of permanence.﴾ [Ghafir: 39] ﴿Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its equivalent, and whoever does righteousness, male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise, being provided therein without account.﴾ [Ghafir: 40] ﴿O my people, what is wrong with me that I invite you to salvation while you invite me to the Fire?﴾ [Ghafir: 41] ﴿You invite me to disbelieve in Allah and to associate with Him what I have no knowledge of, while I invite you to the Mighty, the Forgiving.﴾ [Ghafir: 42] ﴿Undoubtedly, what you invite me to has no call in this world or in the Hereafter, and our return is to Allah, and the transgressors are the companions of the Fire.﴾ [Ghafir: 43] ﴿So you will remember what I say to you. I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed Allah is All-Seeing of the servants.﴾ [Ghafir: 44] ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted, and the terrible punishment encompassed the family of Pharaoh.﴾ [Ghafir: 45] ﴿The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening; and on the Day the Hour is established: "Admit the family of Pharaoh to the severest punishment."﴾ [Ghafir: 46] ﴿And when they argue in the Fire, the weak will say to those who were arrogant: "Indeed we were following you, so will you relieve us of a portion of the Fire?"﴾ [Ghafir: 47] ﴿Those who were arrogant will say: "Indeed we are all in it. Indeed Allah has judged between the servants."﴾ [Ghafir: 48] ﴿And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell: "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of punishment."﴾ [Ghafir: 49] ﴿They will say: "Did your messengers not come to you with clear proofs?" They will say: "Yes." They will say: "Then call upon them." But the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error.﴾ [Ghafir: 50] ﴿Indeed We will help Our messengers and those who believed in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir: 51] ﴿the Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers. For them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode.﴾ [Ghafir: 52] ﴿And We gave Moses guidance, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book﴾ [Ghafir: 53] ﴿as guidance and a reminder for people of understanding.﴾ [Ghafir: 54] ﴿So be patient; indeed the promise of Allah is true. And ask forgiveness for your sin, and glorify your Lord with praise in the evening and the morning.﴾ [Ghafir: 55] ﴿Indeed those who dispute the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them, there is nothing in their chests but pride, which they will never attain. So seek refuge in Allah; indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾ [Ghafir: 56] ﴿Surely the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most people do not know.﴾ [Ghafir: 57] ﴿The blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer. Little do you remember.﴾ [Ghafir: 58] ﴿Indeed the Hour is coming, there is no doubt in it, but most people do not believe.﴾ [Ghafir: 59] ﴿And your Lord says: "Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Indeed those who are too arrogant to worship Me will enter Hell, humiliated."﴾ [Ghafir: 60] ﴿It is Allah who made the night for you that you may rest in it, and the day giving sight. Indeed Allah is full of bounty toward mankind, but most people do not give thanks.﴾ [Ghafir: 61] ﴿That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things. There is no god but Him. So how are you turned away?﴾ [Ghafir: 62] ﴿Thus are turned away those who used to deny the signs of Allah.﴾ [Ghafir: 63] ﴿It is Allah who made the earth a resting place for you and the sky a canopy, and shaped you and perfected your forms, and provided you with good things. That is Allah, your Lord. So blessed is Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [Ghafir: 64] ﴿He is the Living; there is no god but Him. So invoke Him, making your religion sincerely His. Praise belongs to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [Ghafir: 65] ﴿Say: "Indeed I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides Allah, since clear proofs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds."﴾ [Ghafir: 66] ﴿It is He who created you from dust, then from a drop, then from a clinging clot, then brings you out as a child, then that you may reach your maturity, then that you may become elders, though some of you are taken before that, and that you may reach a specified term, and that perhaps you will reason.﴾ [Ghafir: 67] ﴿It is He who gives life and causes death. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ [Ghafir: 68] ﴿Have you not seen those who dispute the signs of Allah? How are they turned away?﴾ [Ghafir: 69] ﴿Those who denied the Book and what We sent with Our messengers; they will soon know﴾ [Ghafir: 70] ﴿when the shackles and chains are around their necks, and they are dragged﴾ [Ghafir: 71] ﴿in the scalding water, then in the Fire they are burned.﴾ [Ghafir: 72]

Azifa al-shay': it drew near. The poet said:
"The time of departure has drawn near, but our mounts have not yet moved from our saddles, and it is as if it had already come."

Al-tabab: ruin. Al-silsila: the chain, which is well known. Al-sahb: dragging. Sajjara al-tannur: I filled the oven with fire.

Ha, Mim. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing; the Forgiver of sin, the Acceptor of repentance, severe in punishment, the Possessor of bounty; there is no god but Him; to Him is the final return. None dispute the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve, so do not let their movement throughout the land deceive you. The people of Noah denied before them, and so did the factions after them; and every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him, and they argued with falsehood to refute the truth by it, so I seized them, and how was My punishment? Thus the word of your Lord has been fulfilled against those who disbelieved: that they are the companions of the Fire.

The Hawamim (the seven surahs beginning with Ha-Mim) are all Meccan, according to unanimous agreement. It has been said that some verses of these surahs are Medinan, but Ibn 'Atiyya said: this is weak.

It is related in a hadith: "The Hawamim are the brocade of the Qur'an." And in it: "Whoever wishes to graze in the pleasant gardens of Paradise, let him recite the Hawamim." And in it: "The likeness of the Hawamim in the Qur'an is like the likeness of the striped patterns in garments."

These Hawamim are devoted to admonition, warning, and the paths of the Hereafter, and they are short, so weariness does not affect them.

The connection of the beginning of this surah to the end of al-Zumar is that when He, the Exalted, mentioned the final state of the disbelievers and the believers, He mentioned here "the Forgiver of sin and the Acceptor of repentance," so that this would be an invitation for the disbeliever to faith, and to giving up what he is engaged in, and to show that the door of repentance is open. He mentioned the severity of His punishment, and that the whole world will be subject to it, so that one would refrain from what he is engaged in, and that his return is to his Lord, who will recompense him for what he does of good or evil.

It is read with a fatha on the ha' (Ha, with the vowel fatha), chosen by Abu al-Qasim ibn Jubara al-Hudhali, author of the book al-Kamil fi al-Qur'an. Abu al-Sammal read it with a kasra, on the basis of the meeting of two unvocalized consonants. Ibn Abi Ishaq and 'Isa read it with a fatha. It has been explained that the fatha is the vowel of meeting of two unvocalized consonants, and that it was a fatha for the sake of lightness, as in "ayna." Or it is an inflectional vowel, governed by an implied verb whose estimated form is: "Recite Ha Mim."

It is related in a hadith that a Bedouin asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about "Ha Mim," what is it? He said: "They are names and openings of surahs." Shurayh ibn Abi Awfa al-Absi said:
"Ha Mim reminds me, while the spear is shaking, so why did he not recite Ha Mim before the advance?"

Al-Kumayt said:
"We found among you, in the family of Hamim, a sign, which a pious and eloquent one interpreted for us."

They inflected "Hamim" and it was not declined (not given tanwin) because of being a proper noun, or because of being a proper noun together with a resemblance to foreign origin, since fa'il is not among the patterns of Arabic word forms, and this is found only in foreign words, like Qabil and Habil.

It has been mentioned in the hadith that "Ha Mim" is pluralized as "Hawamim," just as "Ta Sin" [al-Naml: 1] is pluralized as "Tawasin."

Abu Hayyan's commentary on surah 40, verses 1–6 (part 2 of 3):

Ṣāḥib Zād al-Masīr related on the authority of his teacher Ibn Manṣūr, the linguist, that he said: "It is an error to say, 'I recited the Ḥawāmīm' (al-Ḥawāmīm), for it is not from the speech of the Arabs; the correct form is to say, 'I recited Āl Ḥā Mīm.'" And in a ḥadīth of Ibn Mas'ūd: "If you come upon Āl Ḥamīm, you have come upon meadows, soft and fragrant." End of quotation.

If it is established that the Messenger (ﷺ) actually said, "al-Ḥawāmīm," it would be a proof against those who forbid it. But if it was transmitted by meaning, it is possible that it is a distortion by non-Arabs.

Do you not see Ibn Mas'ūd's wording, "If you come upon Āl Ḥamīm," and the verse of al-Kumayt: "We found for you in Āl Ḥāmīm"? The discussion of these disjoined letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭa'ah) has already passed at the beginning of al-Baqarah. Some have added other opinions concerning Ḥā Mīm here, which are transmitted from the early generations (al-salaf). We have dispensed with mentioning them, because they are confused and there is no evidence for the soundness of any of them.

If Ḥā Mīm is the name of the surah, it occupies a position of nominative (raf') as a subject (mubtadaʾ), and "Tanzīl" is then its predicate with "min Allāh" as the predicate. Otherwise, "Tanzīl" is a subject and "min Allāh" is the predicate; or it is the predicate of an implied subject, i.e., "this is the tanzīl," and "min Allāh" is related to "tanzīl."

﴿al-ʿAzīz al-ʿAlīm﴾: two attributes indicating intensity in power, dominance, and knowledge, and they are among the attributes of the Essence (ṣifāt al-dhāt).

Al-Zajjāj said: "Ghāfir" and "Qābil" are attributes, and "Shadīd" is an apposition (badal). End of quotation.

He made "Ghāfir" and "Qābil" attributes even though they are active participles (ismā fāʿil), because it is understood from them that they are not intended to denote renewal or restriction to a time, but rather continuity and permanence. Their annexation (iḍāfah) is genuine (maḥḍah), so they are definite, and it is correct for a definite noun to be described by them. "Shadīd al-ʿiqāb" is parsed as an apposition because it belongs to the category of the attributive adjective (al-ṣifah al-mushabbahah), which does not become definite through annexation to a definite noun. Sībawayh has explicitly stated that any noun whose annexation is not genuine, when annexed to a definite noun, may be intended as genuine annexation, and thus becomes definite and can describe a definite noun, except for what belongs to the category of the attributive adjective, which does not become definite.

The author of al-Muqniʿ relates from the Kufans that they permitted, in "ḥusn al-wajh" and similar expressions, that it be an attribute of a definite noun. He said: "That is an error according to the Basrans, because ḥusn al-wajh is indefinite, and when you want to define it, you add al-." 

Abu al-Ḥajjāj al-Aʿlam said: "It is not far-fetched that ḥusn al-wajh be intended as definite, since annexation does not prevent it." End of quotation. This is a leaning toward the Kufan position.

Some have made "Ghāfir al-dhanb" and what follows it appositions, considering that they do not become definite through annexation, as if he had regarded the future time in "Ghāfir" and "Qābil."

It has also been said: "Ghāfir" and "Qābil" are not intended to refer to the past; they become definite through annexation and are attributes, meaning that His decree of forgiveness and acceptance of repentance is in this world.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: Al-Zajjāj's making "Shadīd al-ʿiqāb" alone an apposition among the attributes contains a clear flaw. The proper view is to say: since a single indefinite noun is placed among these definite nouns, it indicates that all of them are appositions and not attributes. An example of this is a poem whose feet all come in the form of mustafʿilun; it is judged to be of the rajaz meter. If one foot in it comes as mutafāʿilun, it becomes of the kāmil meter, and there is no flaw in that, because following the established and sound rules is the original principle.

His statement, "it indicates that all of them are appositions," is itself a fault of composition not in Arabic, because he made "fa-qad ādhanat" the answer to "lammā," and it is not from their speech to say: "lammā qāma Zaydun fa-qad qāma ʿAmrun." His statement, "that all of them are appositions," involves repetition of appositions. As for an apposition of an apposition according to those who affirm it, appositions do repeat in it. As for apposition of whole from whole, partial apposition, and apposition of inclusion, I know of no statement from any grammarian permitting or forbidding repetition in them, except that in the words of one of our companions there is something indicating that an apposition is not repeated. That occurs in the verse of the poet:

Then to the son of Umm Unās I ride my she-camel,
ʿAmr, so that my she-camel reaches him or crawls to him.

A king, when the delegations alight at his gate,
they know the sources of his cloud, which do not run dry.

He said: "So 'malik' is an apposition of ʿAmr, an indefinite apposition of a definite noun." He said: "If you say, why is it not an apposition of Ibn Umm Unās? I say: because ʿAmr has already been made an apposition of it, so it is not permissible to make it an apposition again, since it has been dropped." End of quotation.

This indicates that an apposition is not repeated, and the appositive noun is one; and it indicates that an apposition of an apposition is permissible. His statement, "their feet come," is the plural of tif'āl, tif'ūl, tif'ūl, or tif'īl, and none of these patterns is a modified form at the end of the ʿarūḍ; rather its feet are limited, and none of them is among these patterns. So the correct statement would be: "its feet all come as mustafʿilun."

Sībawayh also said: "One may say they are attributes, and the alif and lam were omitted from 'Shadīd al-ʿiqāb' in order to match what precedes and follows it in sound. They have changed much of their speech from its rules for the sake of rhyme (izdiwāj), to the extent that they said: 'mā yaʿrifu suḥādilayhi min ʿanādilayhi,' so they made the dual of what is odd (witr) for the sake of what is even (shaf')." End of quotation.

Moreover, al-Khalīl said, regarding their saying: "It is not fitting for a man like you to do that, and it is fitting for a better man than you to do," that it is intended with the alif and lam, just as "al-jammāʾ al-ghafīr" is intended without the alif and lam. What facilitates this is the absence of confusion and the vagueness of the described noun. End of quotation.

There is no need to believe that the alif and lam were dropped from "Shadīd al-ʿiqāb," abandoning what is fundamental in grammar and likening it to a rare form deviating from the rules, namely the dual of the odd for the even. The Book of God is to be exalted above all of this.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: It may be said that he deliberately made it indefinite and vague, to indicate the extreme severity and that there is nothing more grievous than it, and to increase the warning. It may also be said that this nuance is what motivates choosing apposition over attribute when one follows the path of apposition. End of quotation.

Makkī permitted in "Ghāfir" and "Qābil" apposition, considering them indefinite because of their reference to the future, and attribute, considering them definite because of their reference to the past. Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Rāzī said: There is no dispute that "Ghāfir" and "Qābil" are attributes; they are so because they express the sense of permanence and continuity, and likewise "Shadīd al-ʿiqāb" conveys that, because His attributes are exempt from occurrence and renewal. Its meaning is: that His punishment is such that it is severe, and this meaning is always present; it is not described as having come about after it was not. End of quotation.

This is the statement of one who has not studied grammar or examined it, and it entails that "ḥakīm ʿalīm" in His saying "from the presence of One Wise, All-Knowing" (al-Naml: 6) and "malīk muqtadir" in His saying "in the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful" (al-Qamar: 55) are definite for the sake of exalting His attributes above occurrence and renewal, and because they are attributes that did not come about after they were not; and that the definition of attributes by al-, and their indefiniteness, would be equal. No beginner in grammar would go this way, let alone one who has written on it and presumed to interpret the Book of God.

From this lengthy discussion it emerges that "Ghāfir al-dhanb" and what is conjoined to it, and "Shadīd al-ʿiqāb," are attributes, because what is conjoined to an attribute is an attribute, and all of them are definite according to what has been established; or they are appositions, because what is conjoined to an apposition is an apposition, given that all of them are indefinite.

Or "Ghāfir" and "Qābil" are attributes, and "Shadīd" is an apposition to the definiteness of those two and the indefiniteness of "Shadīd."

Al-Zamakhsharī said: (If you ask): what is the role of the waw in His saying "wa-Qābil al-tawb"? (I answer): in it is a magnificent nuance, namely the gathering for the sinning repentant one of two mercies: that He accepts his repentance and records it for him as one of the acts of obedience, and that He makes it an erasure of sins, as if he had not sinned; as if He said: "Gatherer of forgiveness and acceptance." End of quotation.

How much this man reaches for and bursts into eloquence! What he has conveyed, that the waw is for gathering, is well known from the apparent principles of grammar.

The author of al-Ghunyān said: "It only conjoined them because they are associated and inseparable, one from the other. And 'Shadīd al-ʿiqāb' was cut off from them and not conjoined, because it stands alone." End of quotation. This is a Muʿtazilī inclination.

The doctrine of the People of the Sunnah is that God may forgive the disobedient, even if he does not repent, except for shirk. "Al-tawb" may be understood as a collective noun like "al-dhanb," or as the plural of tawbah, like bashr and bashrah, or sāʿin and sāʿah. The apparent meaning of His saying "wa-Qābil al-tawb" is that the repentance of the disobedient one, short of disbelief, is certainly accepted, just as the repentance of one who has disbelieved.

Regarding the certainty of accepting the repentance of the disobedient, the People of the Sunnah mention two views.

When God mentioned the severity of His punishment, He followed it with what gives hope in His mercy, namely His saying "Dhī al-Ṭawl," so this came as a threat flanked by two promises. Ibn ʿAbbās said: al-ṭawl is abundance and wealth; Qatādah said: blessings; Ibn Zayd said: power. His saying "ṭawlihi" means the multiplication of the good deeds of His friends and His pardon of their evil deeds.

When He mentioned a portion of His supreme attributes, essential and active, He mentioned that He alone is the Deity, and that to Him is the return on the Day of Assembly. Then He mentioned the state of those who dispute concerning the Book, and followed it with mention of the obedient among His angels and righteous servants, saying: ﴿None dispute concerning the signs of God except those who disbelieve﴾. Their disputing about them was saying at one time, "magic," at another, "poetry," at another, "tales of the ancients," and at another, "a human only teaches him." So it is disputation by falsehood, and He indicated this by His saying: ﴿and they disputed by falsehood to refute the truth thereby﴾.

Al-Suddī said: "yujādilu" means "yumārī" (contends). Ibn Salām said: "yajḥadu" (denies). Abū al-ʿĀliyah said: it was revealed concerning al-Ḥārith ibn Qays, one of the mockers.

As for what takes place among the people of knowledge regarding reflection upon them, clarifying their meanings, deriving rulings and beliefs from them, and contending with the people of innovation through them, there is abundant reward in that.

Then He forbade the listener to be deceived by the movement of these disbelievers in the lands and their dealings there, with what I have granted them of dwellings, farms, dominions, trade, and gains; and Quraysh used to trade in Syria and Yemen. For that is a burden upon them and a cause of their destruction, just as those before them who denied the messengers were destroyed.

The majority read ﴿fa-lā yaghrurka﴾ with unassimilated form (bi-l-fakk), and this is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz.

Zayd ibn ʿAlī and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read "fa-lā yaghurrak," with assimilation and a fatḥah on the rāʾ, and this is the dialect of Tamīm.

Since the disputation of the disbelievers arose from denying what the Messenger (peace be upon him) brought of the signs of God, He mentioned those among the earlier nations who denied before them, and what their condition came to of the descent of God's vengeance upon them, so that the disbelievers to whom the Messenger (peace be upon him) was sent might be deterred. So He began with the people of Noah, since he (peace be upon him) was the first messenger on earth, and He joined to his people "al-aḥzāb," who are those who banded together against the messengers and did not accept what they came with from God; among them were ʿĀd, Thamūd, Pharaoh and his followers.

He placed the intention to seize before disputation by falsehood, because when God protected the messengers from them so that they could not kill them, they returned to disputation by falsehood. The majority read ﴿bi-rasūlihim﴾ ("their messenger"); ʿAbd Allāh read "bi-rasūlihā" ("its messenger"), the pronoun referring to the wording "ummah" (community).

﴿li-yaʾkhudhūhu﴾: that they might gain control over him, by imprisonment, torture, or killing. Ibn ʿAbbās said: li-yaʾkhudhūhu means li-yamlikūhu (that they might possess him), and Quṭrub recited:

If you seize me and kill me, how many a seizer has desired my immortality!

It is said of the slain and the captive: "akhīdh." Qatādah said: li-yaʾkhudhūhu means li-yaqtulūhu (that they might kill him), expressing the effect by its cause.

﴿wa-jādalū bi-l-bāṭil﴾: i.e., by that which is vanishing and perishing, having no stability. It was also said: "al-bāṭil" is disbelief; it was said: it is Satan; it was said: by their saying: ﴿You are only human beings like us﴾ (Yā-Sīn: 15).

﴿li-yudḥiḍū bihi al-ḥaqq﴾: that they might cause the truth to slip away; i.e., the firm, true thing.

﴿fa-akhadhtuhum﴾: so I seized them, i.e., I destroyed them.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 40, verse 1–6 (part 3 of 3):

﴿Then how was My punishment﴾ — this is a rhetorical question (istifham ta'ajjub) expressing wonder at their annihilation and magnifying what befell them, not a question about the manner (kayfiyyah) of their punishment. They used to pass by their dwellings and see the traces of God's blessing upon them. He dispensed with the ya' of possession (ya' al-idafah), using the kasrah instead, because it falls at the end of a verse (fasilah); the original form is ʿiqābī.

﴿And thus was it decreed﴾ — i.e., just as that necessity of punishment was incumbent upon those [earlier peoples], so it was incumbent upon the disbelievers, by virtue of their being among the companions of the Fire, both those who came before them and those who came after.

(Annahum): it is a substitute (badal) for ﴿the word of your Lord﴾, so it is in the nominative position (fi mawdi' raf'). It is also permissible that the implied phrase is li-annahum, with the lam of causation (lam al-'illah) omitted. The meaning: just as the destruction of those nations was necessary, so the destruction of these people is necessary, because the cause that necessitates their destruction is a common attribute that unites them, namely their being among the companions of the Fire.

In the codex of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) it reads: "wa-kadhalika sabaqat" (and thus has preceded), which is an interpretation of meaning (tafsir ma'na), not a recitation (qira'ah). Ibn Hurmuz, Shaybah, Ibn al-Qa'qa', Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir recited ﴿kalimat﴾ in the plural; Abu Raja', Qatadah and the rest of the Seven recited it in the singular.

[p. 444]

Surah Ghafir: eighty-five verses. Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿Ha, Mim.﴾ ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing,﴾ ﴿the Forgiver of sin, the Acceptor of repentance, Severe in punishment, the Possessor of bounty. There is no god but Him; to Him is the final return.﴾ ﴿None dispute the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve, so do not let their movement throughout the land deceive you.﴾ ﴿The people of Noah denied before them, and so did the factions after them. And every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him, and they argued with falsehood to refute the truth by it. So I seized them. Then how was My punishment?﴾ ﴿Thus the word of your Lord has been fulfilled against those who disbelieved: that they are the companions of the Fire.﴾ ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with His praise and believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who believe: "Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire.﴾ [Ghafir: 7] ﴿Our Lord, admit them to the Gardens of Eden which You promised them, along with whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring. Indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ [Ghafir: 8] ﴿And protect them from evil deeds. Whoever You protect from evil deeds on that Day, You have truly shown them mercy. That is the great triumph.﴾ [Ghafir: 9] ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve will be called out: "The aversion of Allah towards you is greater than your aversion towards yourselves, when you were called to faith and you disbelieved."﴾ [Ghafir: 10] ﴿They will say: "Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and gave us life twice. So we have acknowledged our sins; is there any way out?"﴾ [Ghafir: 11] ﴿That is because when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved; but when partners were associated with Him, you believed. So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Great.﴾ [Ghafir: 12] ﴿It is He who shows you His signs and sends down provision for you from the sky. But none remember except those who turn back (to Allah).﴾ [Ghafir: 13] ﴿So invoke Allah, making your religion sincerely His, even though the disbelievers dislike it.﴾ [Ghafir: 14] ﴿Lofty in rank, Lord of the Throne, He casts the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants, to warn of the Day of Meeting.﴾ [Ghafir: 15] ﴿The Day when they will come forth, and nothing about them will be hidden from Allah. "Whose is the kingdom today?" "It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer."﴾ [Ghafir: 16] ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. There is no injustice today. Indeed Allah is swift in reckoning.﴾ [Ghafir: 17] ﴿And warn them of the Approaching Day, when hearts will be at the throats, choking with grief. The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend nor any intercessor who will be obeyed.﴾ [Ghafir: 18] ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the chests conceal.﴾ [Ghafir: 19] ﴿And Allah judges with truth, while those they invoke besides Him do not judge anything. Indeed Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾ [Ghafir: 20] ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and in traces left upon the earth, yet Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no protector against Allah.﴾ [Ghafir: 21] ﴿That is because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed He is Strong, Severe in punishment.﴾ [Ghafir: 22] ﴿And We sent Moses with Our signs and clear authority﴾ [Ghafir: 23] ﴿to Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun. They said: "A sorcerer, a liar."﴾ [Ghafir: 24] ﴿When he brought them the truth from Us, they said: "Kill the sons of those who believe with him, and spare their women." But the plotting of the disbelievers is only in error.﴾ [Ghafir: 25] ﴿Pharaoh said: "Leave me to kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed I fear that he will change your religion or that he will cause corruption in the land."﴾ [Ghafir: 26] ﴿Moses said: "I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning."﴾ [Ghafir: 27] ﴿A believing man from Pharaoh's family, who was concealing his faith, said: "Will you kill a man because he says, 'My Lord is Allah,' and he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? If he is a liar, his lie will fall upon him; but if he is truthful, some of what he threatens you with will befall you. Indeed Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar.﴾ [Ghafir: 28] ﴿O my people, yours is the kingdom today, dominant in the land. But who will help us against the might of Allah if it comes upon us?" Pharaoh said: "I only show you what I see, and I guide you only to the path of right conduct."﴾ [Ghafir: 29] ﴿And the one who believed said: "O my people, I fear for you a day like the day of the factions﴾ [Ghafir: 30] ﴿like the custom of the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, and those after them. And Allah does not desire injustice for His servants.﴾ [Ghafir: 31] ﴿O my people, I fear for you the Day of Calling Out﴾ [Ghafir: 32] ﴿the day you will turn your backs fleeing. You will have no protector from Allah, and whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide.﴾ [Ghafir: 33] ﴿Yusuf had already brought you clear proofs before, but you remained in doubt about what he brought you. Then when he died, you said: "Allah will never send a messenger after him." Thus Allah leaves astray whoever is a transgressor and a doubter.﴾ [Ghafir: 34] (p. 445) ﴿Those who dispute the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them, it is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah and of those who believe. Thus Allah seals every heart of an arrogant, tyrannical person.﴾ [Ghafir: 35] ﴿And Pharaoh said: "O Haman, build for me a tower that I may reach the ways﴾ [Ghafir: 36] ﴿the ways to the heavens, and look upon the God of Moses. Indeed I think he is a liar." Thus the evil of his deeds was made attractive to Pharaoh, and he was barred from the way. And the plotting of Pharaoh was nothing but ruin.﴾ [Ghafir: 37] ﴿And the one who believed said: "O my people, follow me, and I will guide you to the path of right conduct.﴾ [Ghafir: 38] ﴿O my people, this worldly life is only a passing enjoyment, and indeed the Hereafter is the abode of permanence.﴾ [Ghafir: 39] ﴿Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its equivalent, and whoever does righteousness, male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise, being provided therein without account.﴾ [Ghafir: 40] ﴿O my people, what is wrong with me that I invite you to salvation while you invite me to the Fire?﴾ [Ghafir: 41] ﴿You invite me to disbelieve in Allah and to associate with Him what I have no knowledge of, while I invite you to the Mighty, the Forgiving.﴾ [Ghafir: 42] ﴿Undoubtedly, what you invite me to has no call in this world or in the Hereafter, and our return is to Allah, and the transgressors are the companions of the Fire.﴾ [Ghafir: 43] ﴿So you will remember what I say to you. I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed Allah is All-Seeing of the servants.﴾ [Ghafir: 44] ﴿So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted, and the terrible punishment encompassed the family of Pharaoh.﴾ [Ghafir: 45] ﴿The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening; and on the Day the Hour is established: "Admit the family of Pharaoh to the severest punishment."﴾ [Ghafir: 46] ﴿And when they argue in the Fire, the weak will say to those who were arrogant: "Indeed we were following you, so will you relieve us of a portion of the Fire?"﴾ [Ghafir: 47] ﴿Those who were arrogant will say: "Indeed we are all in it. Indeed Allah has judged between the servants."﴾ [Ghafir: 48] ﴿And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell: "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of punishment."﴾ [Ghafir: 49] ﴿They will say: "Did your messengers not come to you with clear proofs?" They will say: "Yes." They will say: "Then call upon them." But the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error.﴾ [Ghafir: 50] ﴿Indeed We will help Our messengers and those who believed in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir: 51] ﴿the Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers. For them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode.﴾ [Ghafir: 52] ﴿And We gave Moses guidance, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book﴾ [Ghafir: 53] ﴿as guidance and a reminder for people of understanding.﴾ [Ghafir: 54] ﴿So be patient; indeed the promise of Allah is true. And ask forgiveness for your sin, and glorify your Lord with praise in the evening and the morning.﴾ [Ghafir: 55] ﴿Indeed those who dispute the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them, there is nothing in their chests but pride, which they will never attain. So seek refuge in Allah; indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾ [Ghafir: 56] ﴿Surely the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most people do not know.﴾ [Ghafir: 57] ﴿The blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer. Little do you remember.﴾ [Ghafir: 58] ﴿Indeed the Hour is coming, there is no doubt in it, but most people do not believe.﴾ [Ghafir: 59] ﴿And your Lord says: "Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Indeed those who are too arrogant to worship Me will enter Hell, humiliated."﴾ [Ghafir: 60] ﴿It is Allah who made the night for you that you may rest in it, and the day giving sight. Indeed Allah is full of bounty toward mankind, but most people do not give thanks.﴾ [Ghafir: 61] ﴿That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things. There is no god but Him. So how are you turned away?﴾ [Ghafir: 62] ﴿Thus are turned away those who used to deny the signs of Allah.﴾ [Ghafir: 63] ﴿It is Allah who made the earth a resting place for you and the sky a canopy, and shaped you and perfected your forms, and provided you with good things. That is Allah, your Lord. So blessed is Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [Ghafir: 64] ﴿He is the Living; there is no god but Him. So invoke Him, making your religion sincerely His. Praise belongs to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾ [Ghafir: 65] ﴿Say: "Indeed I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides Allah, since clear proofs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds."﴾ [Ghafir: 66] ﴿It is He who created you from dust, then from a drop, then from a clinging clot, then brings you out as a child, then that you may reach your maturity, then that you may become elders, though some of you are taken before that, and that you may reach a specified term, and that perhaps you will reason.﴾ [Ghafir: 67] ﴿It is He who gives life and causes death. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ [Ghafir: 68] ﴿Have you not seen those who dispute the signs of Allah? How are they turned away?﴾ [Ghafir: 69] ﴿Those who denied the Book and what We sent with Our messengers; they will soon know﴾ [Ghafir: 70] ﴿when the shackles and chains are around their necks, and they are dragged﴾ [Ghafir: 71] ﴿in the scalding water, then in the Fire they are burned.﴾ [Ghafir: 72]

Azifa al-shay': it drew near. The poet said:
"The time of departure has drawn near, but our mounts have not yet moved from our saddles, and it is as if it had already come."

Al-tabab: ruin. Al-silsila: the chain, which is well known. Al-sahb: dragging. Sajjara al-tannur: I filled the oven with fire.

Ha, Mim. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing; the Forgiver of sin, the Acceptor of repentance, severe in punishment, the Possessor of bounty; there is no god but Him; to Him is the final return. None dispute the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve, so do not let their movement throughout the land deceive you. The people of Noah denied before them, and so did the factions after them; and every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him, and they argued with falsehood to refute the truth by it, so I seized them, and how was My punishment? Thus the word of your Lord has been fulfilled against those who disbelieved: that they are the companions of the Fire.

The Hawamim (the seven surahs beginning with Ha-Mim) are all Meccan, according to unanimous agreement. It has been said that some verses of these surahs are Medinan, but Ibn 'Atiyya said: this is weak.

It is related in a hadith: "The Hawamim are the brocade of the Qur'an." And in it: "Whoever wishes to graze in the pleasant gardens of Paradise, let him recite the Hawamim." And in it: "The likeness of the Hawamim in the Qur'an is like the likeness of the striped patterns in garments."

These Hawamim are devoted to admonition, warning, and the paths of the Hereafter, and they are short, so weariness does not affect them.

The connection of the beginning of this surah to the end of al-Zumar is that when He, the Exalted, mentioned the final state of the disbelievers and the believers, He mentioned here "the Forgiver of sin and the Acceptor of repentance," so that this would be an invitation for the disbeliever to faith, and to giving up what he is engaged in, and to show that the door of repentance is open. He mentioned the severity of His punishment, and that the whole world will be subject to it, so that one would refrain from what he is engaged in, and that his return is to his Lord, who will recompense him for what he does of good or evil.

It is read with a fatha on the ha' (Ha, with the vowel fatha), chosen by Abu al-Qasim ibn Jubara al-Hudhali, author of the book al-Kamil fi al-Qur'an. Abu al-Sammal read it with a kasra, on the basis of the meeting of two unvocalized consonants. Ibn Abi Ishaq and 'Isa read it with a fatha. It has been explained that the fatha is the vowel of meeting of two unvocalized consonants, and that it was a fatha for the sake of lightness, as in "ayna." Or it is an inflectional vowel, governed by an implied verb whose estimated form is: "Recite Ha Mim."

It is related in a hadith that a Bedouin asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about "Ha Mim," what is it? He said: "They are names and openings of surahs." Shurayh ibn Abi Awfa al-Absi said:
"Ha Mim reminds me, while the spear is shaking, so why did he not recite Ha Mim before the advance?"

Al-Kumayt said:
"We found among you, in the family of Hamim, a sign, which a pious and eloquent one interpreted for us."

They inflected "Hamim" and it was not declined (not given tanwin) because of being a proper noun, or because of being a proper noun together with a resemblance to foreign origin, since fa'il is not among the patterns of Arabic word forms, and this is found only in foreign words, like Qabil and Habil.

It has been mentioned in the hadith that "Ha Mim" is pluralized as "Hawamim," just as "Ta Sin" [al-Naml: 1] is pluralized as "Tawasin."

Abu Hayyan's commentary on surah 40, verses 1–6 (part 2 of 3):

Ṣāḥib Zād al-Masīr related on the authority of his teacher Ibn Manṣūr, the linguist, that he said: "It is an error to say, 'I recited the Ḥawāmīm' (al-Ḥawāmīm), for it is not from the speech of the Arabs; the correct form is to say, 'I recited Āl Ḥā Mīm.'" And in a ḥadīth of Ibn Mas'ūd: "If you come upon Āl Ḥamīm, you have come upon meadows, soft and fragrant." End of quotation.

If it is established that the Messenger (ﷺ) actually said, "al-Ḥawāmīm," it would be a proof against those who forbid it. But if it was transmitted by meaning, it is possible that it is a distortion by non-Arabs.

Do you not see Ibn Mas'ūd's wording, "If you come upon Āl Ḥamīm," and the verse of al-Kumayt: "We found for you in Āl Ḥāmīm"? The discussion of these disjoined letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭa'ah) has already passed at the beginning of al-Baqarah. Some have added other opinions concerning Ḥā Mīm here, which are transmitted from the early generations (al-salaf). We have dispensed with mentioning them, because they are confused and there is no evidence for the soundness of any of them.

If Ḥā Mīm is the name of the surah, it occupies a position of nominative (raf') as a subject (mubtadaʾ), and "Tanzīl" is then its predicate with "min Allāh" as the predicate. Otherwise, "Tanzīl" is a subject and "min Allāh" is the predicate; or it is the predicate of an implied subject, i.e., "this is the tanzīl," and "min Allāh" is related to "tanzīl."

﴿al-ʿAzīz al-ʿAlīm﴾: two attributes indicating intensity in power, dominance, and knowledge, and they are among the attributes of the Essence (ṣifāt al-dhāt).

Al-Zajjāj said: "Ghāfir" and "Qābil" are attributes, and "Shadīd" is an apposition (badal). End of quotation.

He made "Ghāfir" and "Qābil" attributes even though they are active participles (ismā fāʿil), because it is understood from them that they are not intended to denote renewal or restriction to a time, but rather continuity and permanence.
