So there must be your victory over your enemies. Al-Kalbi said: this was abrogated (nusikha, i.e., superseded by a later ruling) by the verse of the sword.

﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾. Ibn 'Atiyya said: it is possible that this was before Allah Exalted informed him that He had forgiven him what preceded of his sin and what follows; because the verse of this surah is Meccan, while the verse of Surat al-Fath is Medinan and later. It is also possible that the address in this verse is to him, and what is meant is that if he is commanded with this, then others are more deserving of complying with it.

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi said: it is to be understood as repentance from leaving what is superior and preferable. It was also said: what is meant by it is pure worship, as in His saying Exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 194], for granting that thing is obligatory, and then He commanded us to ask for it. It was also said: ﴿for your sin﴾ means for the sin of your community against you.

It was said: He attributed the verbal noun to its object, then He commanded him to glorify Him Exalted at these two times, when people are occupied with their important interests. It is also possible that what is meant is all times, and He expressed that by the two periods of time. Ibn 'Abbas said: by that He meant the five prayers. Qatada said: the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer. Al-Hasan said: two rak'ahs before the prayer was enjoined. And also from al-Hasan: the afternoon prayer and the dawn prayer.

The apparent meaning is that ﴿those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah﴾, which are His proofs that He set up for His oneness and His revealed books, and what He manifested at the hands of His prophets of extraordinary events (kharq al-'adah), are the disbelievers of Quraysh and the Arabs.

﴿Without authority﴾, i.e., without evidence or proof.

﴿There is nothing in their breasts but pride﴾, i.e., arrogance and self-magnification, which is the desire for precedence and leadership. That is what drives them to dispute with falsehood and to refuse what is due to you of precedence over them, because of the prophethood He has granted you and the burdens of messengerhood He has imposed on you.

﴿Which they will never attain﴾, i.e., they will never reach the object and consequence of pride from their leadership and precedence. In this there is an indication that they will not lead, and they will not obtain what they hope for.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: in opposition to your denial, there is nothing in their breasts but pride toward you, and they will never reach what that pride requires, because Allah has humbled them.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: its estimated meaning is: those who will never reach the fulfilment of their desire in it. Muqatil said: this is about the Jews.

Muqatil said: the Jews magnified the Dajjal (the Antichrist), and they said: our companion will be raised at the end of time and will have authority. So Exalted is He said: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah﴾, because the Dajjal is one of His signs, ﴿without authority﴾, i.e., without proof. ﴿So seek refuge in Allah﴾ from the trial of the Dajjal.

What is meant by ﴿the creation of mankind﴾ is the Dajjal. This view was held by Abu al-'Aliyah, and this opinion is the most correct.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It was also said that the disputers are the Jews, and they used to say: our companion, the Messiah son of Dawud (the Messiah, son of David), will come out, meaning the Dajjal, and his authority will reach the land and the sea, and rivers will flow with him, and he is a sign from the signs of Allah; then the kingdom will return to us. So Allah called their wishing for that pride, and denied that they would reach what they wish for. End of quote.

The chief of the Jews in his time in Egypt was Musa ibn Maymun al-Andalusi al-Qurtubi (Maimonides), who had written his letter to the Jews of Yemen that their companion would appear in such-and-such a year and five hundred, and the enemy of Allah lied. That year came and many years after it, and nothing of what he had said appeared, may Allah curse him. This Jew had professed Islam, until some kings of the Maghrib and a man from al-Andalus were deceived. It is reported that he led the people in the tarawih prayers (night prayers in Ramadan) while they were on board a ship in Ramadan, since he had memorised the Qur'an.

When he came to Egypt, and that was during the state of the 'Ubaydiyyin (Fatimids), who did not adhere to any sharia, he returned to Judaism and reported that he had been compelled to become Muslim. That was accepted from him, and he composed works for them, among them: (The Book of the Guide for the Perplexed). He gained what he gained only from his association with the scholars of al-Andalus and his cultivation of their favour. And leadership in Egypt until now belongs to the Jews, in every one of his descendants.

﴿So seek refuge in Allah﴾, i.e., take refuge in Him from the plot of the one who envies you.

﴿Indeed He is the Hearing﴾ of what you say and what they say, ﴿the Seeing﴾ of what you do and what they do. So He is your helper against them and your protector from their evil.

Then Exalted is He alerted that it is not proper for the signs of Allah to be disputed, nor for a person to be proud by his saying: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾, i.e., the created beings are greater and more majestic than the creation of humans, so no one has the right to dispute and be arrogant toward his Creator.

Al-Zamakhshari said: their disputing concerning the sign of Allah involved denying the resurrection, and that is the root of the dispute and its basis. So argue with them by the creation of the heavens and the earth, because they used to acknowledge that Allah created them and that they are a great creation whose measure cannot be estimated. The creation of mankind in comparison to it is a small and humble thing; whoever is able to create them despite their greatness is more able, despite the humility of man, to create the human. This is more eloquent than citing the creation of the like of it. End of quote.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: it is possible that the speech concerns resurrection and re-creation, so Exalted is He informed that He who created the heavens and the earth is strong and able to create mankind again. So the verbal noun (khalq) is attributed to its object.

Al-Naqqash said: the meaning is "of what people create," since in reality they do not own anything; so the verbal noun is attributed to its agent.

﴿But most people do not know﴾, i.e., they do not reflect, because heedlessness overwhelms them. The negation of knowledge from the majority and restricting it to them indicates that a few do know. For this reason He made a parable for the ignorant with the blind, and for the knowing with the seeing. The negation of equality between them is from the aspect that indicates blindness and sight; otherwise they are equal in many respects. When it was far, He divided those who believed by the length of the relative clause. He repeated "not" for emphasis, and He placed ﴿those who believed﴾ first because of its proximity to His saying "the seeing." These are two methods: one is that the matching item is placed adjacent to its counterpart in this way; the other is that what corresponds to the first is placed first and what corresponds to the second is placed later, as in His saying Exalted is He: ﴿And not equal are the blind and the seeing﴾ [Fatir: 19], ﴿nor the darknesses and the light﴾ [Fatir: 20], ﴿nor the shade and the heat﴾ [Fatir: 21]. Sometimes the two similar items are placed later, as in His saying Exalted is He: ﴿The example of the two groups is like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing﴾ [Hud: 24]. All of that is a variety in eloquence and styles of speech.

Since His saying ﴿But most people do not know﴾ had already preceded, and that was a description of blame, it was appropriate to begin the mention of equality with a description of blame, so He began with the blind. Qatada, Talha, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, 'Isa, and the Kufans read ﴿tatadhakkarun﴾ (you remember) with the second-person prefix (ta); the majority, al-A'raj, al-Hasan, Abu Ja'far, and Shayba read it with the third-person prefix (ya), as the absent form.

Then He informed of what indicates the resurrection, namely the coming of the Hour, and that there is no doubt about its occurrence. It is the Day of Resurrection, when judgement takes place and the gathering separates: the obedient to Paradise, the disbelievers to the Fire, and those among the disobedient whom Allah wills to punish, other than for disbelief.

The apparent meaning is to take supplication and response in their literal senses, except that the response is conditioned by the will of Allah.

Al-Suddi said: "Ask Me, I will give you." Al-Dahhak said: "Obey Me, I will give you." A group including Mujahid said: "Call upon Me" means "worship Me," and "I will respond to you" means "I will give you in return for worship."

Supplication is often used in the Qur'an with the meaning of worship, and this interpretation is strengthened by His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me﴾. And what al-Nu'man ibn Bashir narrated, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Supplication is worship," and he recited this verse. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Declare My oneness, and I will forgive you." It was said to al-Thawri: "Call upon Allah, Exalted is He." He said: "Abandoning sins is supplication." Al-Hasan, when asked about this verse, said: "Act and rejoice, for it is a truth upon Allah that He answers those who believe and do righteous deeds, and increases them from His bounty." Anas said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Let each of you ask his Lord for his need, all of it, even the thong of his sandal."

﴿Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me﴾, i.e., to supplicate to Me.

The majority of the seven readers, al-Hasan, and Shayba read ﴿sayadkhulun﴾ (they will enter) in the active voice; Zayd ibn 'Ali, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Ja'far read it in the passive voice; there is a difference of report from 'Asim and Abu 'Amr.

﴿Dakhirin﴾: humiliated.

﴿Allah is the One who made the night for you that you may rest therein, and the day giving sight﴾: The discussion of a sentence like this has already preceded in Surat Yunus. And ﴿la-dhu fadl﴾ (full of bounty) is more emphatic than "la-mufaddal" or "la-mutafaddil," as in His saying: ﴿Indeed he is a possessor of knowledge through what We have taught him﴾ [Yusuf: 68], ﴿Let the one of wealth spend from his wealth﴾ [al-Talaq: 7], and ﴿And Allah is the possessor of great bounty﴾; because it indicates that he is its possessor and is empowered by it, unlike when the attribute is expressed, which may indicate attribution to someone other than Allah by being characterised by it at some time, not permanently. He mentioned the generality of His bounty and its provision to people, then He said: ﴿But most people﴾, presenting it explicitly, and He did not use the construction "but most of them."

Al-Zamakhshari said: in this repetition there is a specification of ingratitude for blessings by them, and that they are the ones who deny Allah's bounty and do not thank Him, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is ungrateful﴾, ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾ [al-'Adiyat: 6], ﴿Indeed, mankind is a great wrongdoer and disbeliever﴾ [Ibrahim: 34]. End of quote.

﴿That﴾, i.e., the One specified by those attributes, distinguished by them: by His response to your supplication, by His making the night and the day as He mentioned, and by His bounty upon you.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 40, verse 53–65 (part 2 of 2):

﴿Allah is your Lord﴾: the one who combines these attributes of divinity (uluhiyyah) and lordship (ruburiyyah), the origination of things (insha' al-ashya') and oneness (wahdaniyyah).

So how are you turned away from worshipping the One whose attributes are these, to worshipping idols? Zayd ibn 'Ali recited (khaliqa) with a fatha on the qaf, and Talhah, in one transmission, recited (yu'faku-na) with the third-person ya' (of absence). The majority (al-Jumhur) recited it with a damma on the qaf and the second-person ta' (of address).

Al-Zamakhshari said: (khaliqa) is in the accusative by way of specification (al-ikhtisas), (kadhalika), meaning: like that turning away, Allah turned away the hearts of those who denied the signs of Allah among the nations from the path of guidance.

When the Exalted mentioned what He had bestowed upon them of night and day, He also mentioned what He had bestowed upon them of making the earth a resting place (mustaqarran) and the sky a building (bina'), that is, a dome (qubbah). From this comes the word (abniyat al-'Arab), the tents of the Arabs for their encampments, because the sky, to the eye, appears like a dome erected over the face of the earth.

The majority recited (suwarakum) with a damma on the sad. Al-A'mash and Abu Razin recited it with a kasra on it, to flee from the damma before the waw, as a dispreference (istithqal). The plural of (fu'lah) with a damma on the fa' following the pattern (fi'al) with a kasra is anomalous (shadhdh), and they said (quwwah) and (qiwa) with a kasra on the qaf, also as an anomaly. It has been said: He did not create any living being with a more beautiful form than the human being.

It has also been said: He did not create them upside down like cattle, as in His saying: ﴿in the best of stature﴾ [al-Tin: 4]. A group recited (suwarakum) with a damma on the sad and a sukun on the waw, following the pattern of (busrah) and (busr).

﴿And He provided you with good things﴾: He bestowed upon them what sustains the upkeep (awd) of their forms. The good things (al-tayyibat) are the pleasurable things in taste, clothing and earnings.

Ibn 'Abbas said: whoever says "There is no god but Allah," let him say immediately after it: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said something similar, then he recited the verse.

(p-474) ﴿Say: "I have been forbidden to worship those you call upon besides God, now that the clear proofs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds."﴾ ﴿It is He who created you from dust, then from a drop of semen, then from a clinging clot, then He brings you forth as an infant, then that you may reach your full strength, then that you may become old men; and among you is one who dies before that, and that you may reach an appointed term, and perhaps you will understand.﴾ ﴿It is He who gives life and causes death. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ ﴿Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of God? How are they turned away?﴾ ﴿Those who denied the Book and what We sent with Our messengers. They will come to know.﴾ ﴿When the shackles are around their necks and the chains, they are dragged,﴾ ﴿into the boiling water, then in the Fire they are kindled.﴾ ﴿Then it is said to them, "Where are those you used to associate with God?"﴾ ﴿They say, "They have strayed from us. Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before." Thus God leads astray the disbelievers.﴾ ﴿That is because you used to exult in the land without right, and because you used to be insolent.﴾ ﴿Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein. How evil is the abode of the arrogant.﴾

God commanded His Prophet, peace be upon him, to inform them that he had been forbidden to worship their idols when the clear proofs had come to him from his Lord. This is a prohibition by revelation (sam'), although it is also forbidden by the proofs of reason ('aql). The proofs of revelation and the proofs of reason thus converge on the prohibition of worshipping idols.

Among the proofs of revelation is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Do you worship what you carve?﴾ [al-Saffat: 95] ﴿While God created you and what you do?﴾ [al-Saffat: 96], and others besides. Mentioning that it is a prohibition by revelation does not indicate that it was not also forbidden by the proofs of reason. When he was forbidden to worship idols, he informed them that he had been commanded to submit to God, Exalted is He. Then he clarified the matter of unity (wahdaniyya) and divinity (uluhiyya), of which their idols are devoid in any respect, by considering the stages of the son of Adam's creation, beginning with his first origin, which is dust.

Then he pointed to procreation by His creating him from a drop of semen. "Child" (tifl) is a collective noun (ism jins), or the meaning is: "then He brings you forth," i.e., each one of you as a child. The discussion of reaching full strength (bulugh al-ashudd) has already been presented.

As for "min qabl" (before that), Mujahid said: "before one becomes an old man." It has been said that it may also mean before these states, when one comes forth as a miscarriage. It has also been said that it is an expression of his being subject to the stages mentioned, and it is not restricted to what precedes old age; rather, some of them die before being brought forth as infants, another before reaching full strength, and another before old age.

﴿And that you may reach﴾ is connected to an elided element, meaning: He keeps you alive so that you may reach, i.e., so that each one of you may reach an appointed term that he does not exceed. Mujahid said: "It refers to the death of all." It has been said that it is the Day of Resurrection. As for "perhaps you will understand," it refers to the lesson and proofs contained in this, if you reflect upon it and ponder it.

When He mentioned the stages of existence, He mentioned that He is the One characterized by giving life and causing death, and that whenever His will becomes related to the bringing into existence of a thing, He brings it into existence without delay. The discussion of similar sentences has already been presented.

Then, after these signs became manifest, He said: Do you not marvel at those who dispute the mission of the Messenger, peace be upon him, and the Book that he brought? This is shown by His saying: ﴿those who denied the Book and what We sent with Our messengers﴾. Then He threatened them with His saying: ﴿They will come to know﴾. This is the view of the majority.

Muhammad ibn Sirin and others said: it is an allusion to the people of desires (ahl al-ahwa') from among the community. They related a hadith to this effect and said: it refers to the people of qadar (divine decree and human will) and those who follow their path. It follows for those who hold this view that His saying ﴿those who denied﴾ be taken as a new independent statement about the disbelievers, with ﴿those who denied﴾ as the subject and ﴿They will come to know﴾ as its predicate. As for the apparent reading, ﴿those who﴾ is a substitute (badal) for the preceding ﴿those who﴾, or the predicate of an elided subject, or in the accusative by way of censure. And "idh" (when) is an adverb of time referring to the past, so the future verb does not govern it, just as one does not say "sa-aqumu amsi" (I will stand yesterday). It has been said that "idh" here takes the place of "idha" (whenever), and that its position is metaphorical; so "idh" here means "idha," and the certainty of the event's occurrence justified this, and it was expressed in the past tense even though the meaning is future.

Al-Nakha'i said: If one shackle of the shackles of Hell were placed upon a mountain, it would drag it until it reached the black water.

He recited ﴿wa-l-salasilu﴾ (and the chains) as a coordination with ﴿al-aghlal﴾ (the shackles), with ﴿yus'habun﴾ (they are dragged) in the passive voice.

Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Zayd ibn 'Ali, Ibn Wathhab, and al-Musi' in his choice of reading recited (p-475) ﴿wa-l-salasila﴾ with the accusative as the object, and ﴿yus'habun﴾ in the active voice. This is the coordination of a verbal sentence upon a nominal sentence.

A group, including Ibn 'Abbas, recited (wa-l-salasili) with the lam in the genitive. Ibn 'Atiyya said: this is by way of an assumed construction, "when their necks are in the shackles and the chains," so it coordinates upon the intended meaning of the speech and not upon the arrangement of the wording, since its arrangement in that case is inverted. This is in the manner of the Arabs' saying: "I put the qalansuwa (cap) on my head," and in the codex of Ubayy: (and in the chains they are dragged).

Al-Zamakhshari said: The reasoning is that if one were to say, "when their necks are in the shackles," in place of His saying ﴿when the shackles are around their necks﴾, it would be correct and sound. Since the two expressions are interchangeable, His saying ﴿wa-l-salasilu﴾ is taken as referring to the other expression. A similar example is the saying of the poet:

Ill-omened ones, they do not reform a tribe, nor a crier except with the separation of its crow.

It is as if it were said: "with those who reform." And it was recited (wa-bi-l-salasili). The end of his words. This is called "coordination upon an assumed construction" ('atf 'ala al-tawahhum). But the assumption of inserting a prepositional particle before "muslihin" is closer than altering the entire structure of the sentence, while the recitation alters the entire structure of the preceding sentence. A similar example is the saying of the poet:

Are you truly going to see, by the Thu'aylibat (a place), nor a desert (baydaa') bearing a swift camel that carries?
Nor one who overtakes while the night is young, with a loaded camel, among the rugged parts of the valley.

The assumed construction is: "you are not innocent, nor one who overtakes."

What Ibn 'Atiyya and al-Zamakhshari said was preceded by al-Farra', who said: Whoever puts "salasil" in the genitive has taken it according to the meaning, because the meaning is: their necks are in the shackles and the chains.

Al-Zajjaj said: Whoever reads "wa-l-salasili" with the genitive, the meaning according to him is: "and in the chains they are dragged."

Ibn al-Anbari said: The genitive on this meaning is not permissible. If you say, "Zayd is in the house," it is not good to omit the preposition and say "Zayd the house." Then he mentioned al-Farra's interpretation, and explained the recitation, and then said: as you say, "'Abd Allah contended with Zayd, the two wise ones (al-'aqilayn)," with the accusative and nominative of al-'aqilayn, because when one of them contends with his companion, the other has contended with him. The end.

This matter is not permissible according to the Basran grammarians, and its permissibility is reported from Muhammad ibn Sa'fan al-Kufi, who said: because each of the two is both agent and object. And it is recited: (wa-bi-l-salasili yus'habun). Perhaps this recitation led al-Zajjaj to interpret the genitive as implying an elided preposition, which is an anomalous interpretation.

Ibn 'Abbas said, regarding the reading of the one who put ﴿wa-l-salasila﴾ in the accusative and opened the ya' of (yas'habun): if they drag them, it is harder for them; they are burdened with this while unable to bear it.

Mujahid said: ﴿yusjarun﴾ (they are kindled) means: they are thrown into it, and so they become fuel for it. Al-Suddi said: ﴿yusjarun﴾ means they are burned.

Then God, Exalted is He, informed that they will be made to stand on the Day of Resurrection for rebuke and reproach. It will be said to them: "Where are the idols that you used to worship in the world?" They will say: ﴿They have strayed from us﴾, i.e., they have been lost to us, vanished, and disappeared. Then their statements become confused, and they resort to lying, saying: ﴿Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before.﴾ This is among the greatest confusion of mind and reasoning.

When it became clear to them that they had been nothing, and that their worship of them had achieved nothing, just as you say: "I thought that so-and-so was something, but when you test him he is nothing, so you find no reward from him."

Their saying ﴿They have strayed from us﴾, together with His saying ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell; you will be coming to it﴾ [al-Anbiya': 98], may be understood to mean that this occurs during their rebuke, so the idols were not with them at that time; or, when they did not benefit them, they said ﴿They have strayed from us﴾, even if they were with them.

﴿Thus﴾ means: like this quality and in this order, ﴿God leads astray the disbelievers.﴾ Al-Zamakhshari said: i.e., like the straying of their gods from them; He leads them astray from their gods, so that even if they sought the gods, or the gods sought them, they would not meet.

That leading astray is because of what you used to have of exultation and insolence, ﴿without right﴾, which is polytheism and worship of idols.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: That punishment in which you are is because of what you used to exult in on earth through sins and disbelief. The end.

As for ﴿tamrahun﴾ (you are insolent), Ibn 'Abbas said: it is boasting and arrogance; Mujahid said: it is pride and frivolity. The end. He said this to them as rebuke, meaning: this is because of what you used to display in the world of joy in sins and abundance of wealth, followers, and health.

Al-Dahhak said: "al-farah" is joy and delight, and "al-maraḥ" is transgression. In a hadith: "God hates the exulting, arrogant ones, and loves every grieving heart."

﴿Tafrahun﴾ and ﴿tamrahun﴾ are from the type of paronomasia by alteration (tajnis al-tahrif), mentioned in the science of rhetorical embellishment (ilm al-badi'), which is when a letter distinguishes between two words.

﴿Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein.﴾ The apparent meaning is that it is said to them: "Enter," after the preceding dialogue, and they had already been in the Fire; but this is a command restricted by "abiding," which is a lasting dwelling, so it is not a command for mere entry. Or, after entering it, they are commanded to enter the seven gates, for each gate has a specified portion of the disbelievers; this command to enter thus implies division into each gate.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Enter﴾ means: it is said to them before this dialogue, at the beginning of the matter: "Enter," because this address is only after they have entered, and at the time when the shackles are on their necks.

The gates of Hell are the seven leading to its layers and its seven levels. The end.

﴿Abiding﴾ is a circumstantial clause of anticipated state (hal muqaddara), and it indicates lasting dwelling. Thus the construction comes: ﴿How evil is the abode of the arrogant﴾; the meaning is: how evil is the entrance of the arrogant, because entry itself does not last, so he did not exaggerate in condemning it, unlike lasting dwelling.

(p-474) ﴿Say: "I have been forbidden to worship those you call upon besides God, now that the clear proofs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds."﴾ ﴿It is He who created you from dust, then from a drop of semen, then from a clinging clot, then He brings you forth as an infant, then that you may reach your full strength, then that you may become old men; and among you is one who dies before that, and that you may reach an appointed term, and perhaps you will understand.﴾ ﴿It is He who gives life and causes death. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ ﴿Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of God? How are they turned away?﴾ ﴿Those who denied the Book and what We sent with Our messengers. They will come to know.﴾ ﴿When the shackles are around their necks and the chains, they are dragged,﴾ ﴿into the boiling water, then in the Fire they are kindled.﴾ ﴿Then it is said to them, "Where are those you used to associate with God?"﴾ ﴿They say, "They have strayed from us. Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before." Thus God leads astray the disbelievers.﴾ ﴿That is because you used to exult in the land without right, and because you used to be insolent.﴾ ﴿Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein. How evil is the abode of the arrogant.﴾

God commanded His Prophet, peace be upon him, to inform them that he had been forbidden to worship their idols when the clear proofs had come to him from his Lord. This is a prohibition by revelation (sam'), although it is also forbidden by the proofs of reason ('aql). The proofs of revelation and the proofs of reason thus converge on the prohibition of worshipping idols.

Among the proofs of revelation is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Do you worship what you carve?﴾ [al-Saffat: 95] ﴿While God created you and what you do?﴾ [al-Saffat: 96], and others besides. Mentioning that it is a prohibition by revelation does not indicate that it was not also forbidden by the proofs of reason. When he was forbidden to worship idols, he informed them that he had been commanded to submit to God, Exalted is He. Then he clarified the matter of unity (wahdaniyya) and divinity (uluhiyya), of which their idols are devoid in any respect, by considering the stages of the son of Adam's creation, beginning with his first origin, which is dust.

Then he pointed to procreation by His creating him from a drop of semen. "Child" (tifl) is a collective noun (ism jins), or the meaning is: "then He brings you forth," i.e., each one of you as a child. The discussion of reaching full strength (bulugh al-ashudd) has already been presented.

As for "min qabl" (before that), Mujahid said: "before one becomes an old man." It has been said that it may also mean before these states, when one comes forth as a miscarriage. It has also been said that it is an expression of his being subject to the stages mentioned, and it is not restricted to what precedes old age; rather, some of them die before being brought forth as infants, another before reaching full strength, and another before old age.

﴿And that you may reach﴾ is connected to an elided element, meaning: He keeps you alive so that you may reach, i.e., so that each one of you may reach an appointed term that he does not exceed. Mujahid said: "It refers to the death of all." It has been said that it is the Day of Resurrection. As for "perhaps you will understand," it refers to the lesson and proofs contained in this, if you reflect upon it and ponder it.

When He mentioned the stages of existence, He mentioned that He is the One characterized by giving life and causing death, and that whenever His will becomes related to the bringing into existence of a thing, He brings it into existence without delay. The discussion of similar sentences has already been presented.

Then, after these signs became manifest, He said: Do you not marvel at those who dispute the mission of the Messenger, peace be upon him, and the Book that he brought? This is shown by His saying: ﴿those who denied the Book and what We sent with Our messengers﴾. Then He threatened them with His saying: ﴿They will come to know﴾. This is the view of the majority.

Muhammad ibn Sirin and others said: it is an allusion to the people of desires (ahl al-ahwa') from among the community. They related a hadith to this effect and said: it refers to the people of qadar (divine decree and human will) and those who follow their path. It follows for those who hold this view that His saying ﴿those who denied﴾ be taken as a new independent statement about the disbelievers, with ﴿those who denied﴾ as the subject and ﴿They will come to know﴾ as its predicate. As for the apparent reading, ﴿those who﴾ is a substitute (badal) for the preceding ﴿those who﴾, or the predicate of an elided subject, or in the accusative by way of censure. And "idh" (when) is an adverb of time referring to the past, so the future verb does not govern it, just as one does not say "sa-aqumu amsi" (I will stand yesterday). It has been said that "idh" here takes the place of "idha" (whenever), and that its position is metaphorical; so "idh" here means "idha," and the certainty of the event's occurrence justified this, and it was expressed in the past tense even though the meaning is future.

Al-Nakha'i said: If one shackle of the shackles of Hell were placed upon a mountain, it would drag it until it reached the black water.

He recited ﴿wa-l-salasilu﴾ (and the chains) as a coordination with ﴿al-aghlal﴾ (the shackles), with ﴿yus'habun﴾ (they are dragged) in the passive voice.

Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Zayd ibn 'Ali, Ibn Wathhab, and al-Musi' in his choice of reading recited (p-475) ﴿wa-l-salasila﴾ with the accusative as the object, and ﴿yus'habun﴾ in the active voice. This is the coordination of a verbal sentence upon a nominal sentence.

A group, including Ibn 'Abbas, recited (wa-l-salasili) with the lam in the genitive. Ibn 'Atiyya said: this is by way of an assumed construction, "when their necks are in the shackles and the chains," so it coordinates upon the intended meaning of the speech and not upon the arrangement of the wording, since its arrangement in that case is inverted. This is in the manner of the Arabs' saying: "I put the qalansuwa (cap) on my head," and in the codex of Ubayy: (and in the chains they are dragged).

Al-Zamakhshari said: The reasoning is that if one were to say, "when their necks are in the shackles," in place of His saying ﴿when the shackles are around their necks﴾, it would be correct and sound. Since the two expressions are interchangeable, His saying ﴿wa-l-salasilu﴾ is taken as referring to the other expression. A similar example is the saying of the poet:

Ill-omened ones, they do not reform a tribe, nor a crier except with the separation of its crow.

It is as if it were said: "with those who reform." And it was recited (wa-bi-l-salasili). The end of his words. This is called "coordination upon an assumed construction" ('atf 'ala al-tawahhum). But the assumption of inserting a prepositional particle before "muslihin" is closer than altering the entire structure of the sentence, while the recitation alters the entire structure of the preceding sentence. A similar example is the saying of the poet:

Are you truly going to see, by the Thu'aylibat (a place), nor a desert (baydaa') bearing a swift camel that carries?
Nor one who overtakes while the night is young, with a loaded camel, among the rugged parts of the valley.

The assumed construction is: "you are not innocent, nor one who overtakes."

What Ibn 'Atiyya and al-Zamakhshari said was preceded by al-Farra', who said: Whoever puts "salasil" in the genitive has taken it according to the meaning, because the meaning is: their necks are in the shackles and the chains.

Al-Zajjaj said: Whoever reads "wa-l-salasili" with the genitive, the meaning according to him is: "and in the chains they are dragged."

Ibn al-Anbari said: The genitive on this meaning is not permissible. If you say, "Zayd is in the house," it is not good to omit the preposition and say "Zayd the house." Then he mentioned al-Farra's interpretation, and explained the recitation, and then said: as you say, "'Abd Allah contended with Zayd, the two wise ones (al-'aqilayn)," with the accusative and nominative of al-'aqilayn, because when one of them contends with his companion, the other has contended with him. The end.

This matter is not permissible according to the Basran grammarians, and its permissibility is reported from Muhammad ibn Sa'fan al-Kufi, who said: because each of the two is both agent and object. And it is recited: (wa-bi-l-salasili yus'habun). Perhaps this recitation led al-Zajjaj to interpret the genitive as implying an elided preposition, which is an anomalous interpretation.

Ibn 'Abbas said, regarding the reading of the one who put ﴿wa-l-salasila﴾ in the accusative and opened the ya' of (yas'habun): if they drag them, it is harder for them; they are burdened with this while unable to bear it.

Mujahid said: ﴿yusjarun﴾ (they are kindled) means: they are thrown into it, and so they become fuel for it. Al-Suddi said: ﴿yusjarun﴾ means they are burned.

Then God, Exalted is He, informed that they will be made to stand on the Day of Resurrection for rebuke and reproach. It will be said to them: "Where are the idols that you used to worship in the world?" They will say: ﴿They have strayed from us﴾, i.e., they have been lost to us, vanished, and disappeared. Then their statements become confused, and they resort to lying, saying: ﴿Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before.﴾ This is among the greatest confusion of mind and reasoning.

When it became clear to them that they had been nothing, and that their worship of them had achieved nothing, just as you say: "I thought that so-and-so was something, but when you test him he is nothing, so you find no reward from him."

Their saying ﴿They have strayed from us﴾, together with His saying ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell; you will be coming to it﴾ [al-Anbiya': 98], may be understood to mean that this occurs during their rebuke, so the idols were not with them at that time; or, when they did not benefit them, they said ﴿They have strayed from us﴾, even if they were with them.

﴿Thus﴾ means: like this quality and in this order, ﴿God leads astray the disbelievers.﴾ Al-Zamakhshari said: i.e., like the straying of their gods from them; He leads them astray from their gods, so that even if they sought the gods, or the gods sought them, they would not meet.

That leading astray is because of what you used to have of exultation and insolence, ﴿without right﴾, which is polytheism and worship of idols.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: That punishment in which you are is because of what you used to exult in on earth through sins and disbelief. The end.

As for ﴿tamrahun﴾ (you are insolent), Ibn 'Abbas said: it is boasting and arrogance; Mujahid said: it is pride and frivolity. The end. He said this to them as rebuke, meaning: this is because of what you used to display in the world of joy in sins and abundance of wealth, followers, and health.

Al-Dahhak said: "al-farah" is joy and delight, and "al-maraḥ" is transgression. In a hadith: "God hates the exulting, arrogant ones, and loves every grieving heart."

﴿Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein.﴾ The apparent meaning is that it is said to them: "Enter," after the preceding dialogue, and they had already been in the Fire; but this is a command restricted by "abiding," which is a lasting dwelling, so it is not a command for mere entry. Or, after entering it, they are commanded to enter the seven gates, for each gate has a specified portion of the disbelievers; this command to enter thus implies division into each gate.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: this is by way of an assumed construction, "when their necks are in the shackles and the chains," so it coordinates upon the intended meaning of the speech and not upon the arrangement of the wording, since its arrangement in that case is inverted. This is in the manner of the Arabs' saying: "I put the qalansuwa (cap) on my head," and in the codex of Ubayy: (and in the chains they are dragged).

Al-Zamakhshari said: The reasoning is that if one were to say, "when their necks are in the shackles," in place of His saying ﴿when the shackles are around their necks﴾, it would be correct and sound. Since the two expressions are interchangeable, His saying ﴿wa-l-salasilu﴾ is taken as referring to the other expression. A similar example is the saying of the poet:

Ill-omened ones, they do not reform a tribe, nor a crier except with the separation of its crow.

It is as if it were said: "with those who reform." And it was recited (wa-bi-l-salasili). The end of his words. This is called "coordination upon an assumed construction" ('atf 'ala al-tawahhum). But the assumption of inserting a prepositional particle before "muslihin" is closer than altering the entire structure of the sentence, while the recitation alters the entire structure of the preceding sentence. A similar example is the saying of the poet:

Are you truly going to see, by the Thu'aylibat (a place), nor a desert (baydaa') bearing a swift camel that carries?
Nor one who overtakes while the night is young, with a loaded camel, among the rugged parts of the valley.

The assumed construction is: "you are not innocent, nor one who overtakes."

What Ibn 'Atiyya and al-Zamakhshari said was preceded by al-Farra', who said: Whoever puts "salasil" in the genitive has taken it according to the meaning, because the meaning is: their necks are in the shackles and the chains.

Al-Zajjaj said: Whoever reads "wa-l-salasili" with the genitive, the meaning according to him is: "and in the chains they are dragged."

Ibn al-Anbari said: The genitive on this meaning is not permissible. If you say, "Zayd is in the house," it is not good to omit the preposition and say "Zayd the house." Then he mentioned al-Farra's interpretation, and explained the recitation, and then said: as you say, "'Abd Allah contended with Zayd, the two wise ones (al-'aqilayn)," with the accusative and nominative of al-'aqilayn, because when one of them contends with his companion, the other has contended with him. The end.

This matter is not permissible according to the Basran grammarians, and its permissibility is reported from Muhammad ibn Sa'fan al-Kufi, who said: because each of the two is both agent and object. And it is recited: (wa-bi-l-salasili yus'habun). Perhaps this recitation led al-Zajjaj to interpret the genitive as implying an elided preposition, which is an anomalous interpretation.

Ibn 'Abbas said, regarding the reading of the one who put ﴿wa-l-salasila﴾ in the accusative and opened the ya' of (yas'habun): if they drag them, it is harder for them; they are burdened with this while unable to bear it.

Mujahid said: ﴿yusjarun﴾ (they are kindled) means: they are thrown into it, and so they become fuel for it. Al-Suddi said: ﴿yusjarun﴾ means they are burned.

Then God, Exalted is He, informed that they will be made to stand on the Day of Resurrection for rebuke and reproach. It will be said to them: "Where are the idols that you used to worship in the world?" They will say: ﴿They have strayed from us﴾, i.e., they have been lost to us, vanished, and disappeared. Then their statements become confused, and they resort to lying, saying: ﴿Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before.﴾ This is among the greatest confusion of mind and reasoning.

When it became clear to them that they had been nothing, and that their worship of them had achieved nothing, just as you say: "I thought that so-and-so was something, but when you test him he is nothing, so you find no reward from him."

Their saying ﴿They have strayed from us﴾, together with His saying ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell; you will be coming to it﴾ [al-Anbiya': 98], may be understood to mean that this occurs during their rebuke, so the idols were not with them at that time; or, when they did not benefit them, they said ﴿They have strayed from us﴾, even if they were with them.

﴿Thus﴾ means: like this quality and in this order, ﴿God leads astray the disbelievers.﴾ Al-Zamakhshari said: i.e., like the straying of their gods from them; He leads them astray from their gods, so that even if they sought the gods, or the gods sought them, they would not meet.

That leading astray is because of what you used to have of exultation and insolence, ﴿without right﴾, which is polytheism and worship of idols.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: That punishment in which you are is because of what you used to exult in on earth through sins and disbelief. The end.

As for ﴿tamrahun﴾ (you are insolent), Ibn 'Abbas said: it is boasting and arrogance; Mujahid said: it is pride and frivolity. The end. He said this to them as rebuke, meaning: this is because of what you used to display in the world of joy in sins and abundance of wealth, followers, and health.

Al-Dahhak said: "al-farah" is joy and delight, and "al-maraḥ" is transgression. In a hadith: "God hates the exulting, arrogant ones, and loves every grieving heart."

﴿Tafrahun﴾ and ﴿tamrahun﴾ are from the type of paronomasia by alteration (tajnis al-tahrif), mentioned in the science of rhetorical embellishment (ilm al-badi'), which is when a letter distinguishes between two words.

﴿Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein.﴾ The apparent meaning is that it is said to them: "Enter," after the preceding dialogue, and they had already been in the Fire; but this is a command restricted by "abiding," which is a lasting dwelling, so it is not a command for mere entry. Or, after entering it, they are commanded to enter the seven gates, for each gate has a specified portion of the disbelievers; this command to enter thus implies division into each gate.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Enter﴾ means: it is said to them before this dialogue, at the beginning of the matter: "Enter," because this address is only after they have entered, and at the time when the shackles are on their necks.

The gates of Hell are the seven leading to its layers and its seven levels. The end.

﴿Abiding﴾ is a circumstantial clause of anticipated state (hal muqaddara), and it indicates lasting dwelling. Thus the construction comes: ﴿How evil is the abode of the arrogant﴾; the meaning is: how evil is the entrance of the arrogant, because entry itself does not last, so he did not exaggerate in condemning it, unlike lasting dwelling.

(p-474) ﴿Say: "I have been forbidden to worship those you call upon besides God, now that the clear proofs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds."﴾ ﴿It is He who created you from dust, then from a drop of semen, then from a clinging clot, then He brings you forth as an infant, then that you may reach your full strength, then that you may become old men; and among you is one who dies before that, and that you may reach an appointed term, and perhaps you will understand.﴾ ﴿It is He who gives life and causes death. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ ﴿Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of God? How are they turned away?﴾ ﴿Those who denied the Book and what We sent with Our messengers. They will come to know.﴾ ﴿When the shackles are around their necks and the chains, they are dragged,﴾ ﴿into the boiling water, then in the Fire they are kindled.﴾ ﴿Then it is said to them, "Where are those you used to associate with God?"﴾ ﴿They say, "They have strayed from us. Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before." Thus God leads astray the disbelievers.﴾ ﴿That is because you used to exult in the land without right, and because you used to be insolent.﴾ ﴿Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein. How evil is the abode of the arrogant.﴾

God commanded His Prophet, peace be upon him, to inform them that he had been forbidden to worship their idols when the clear proofs had come to him from his Lord. This is a prohibition by revelation (sam'), although it is also forbidden by the proofs of reason ('aql). The proofs of revelation and the proofs of reason thus converge on the prohibition of worshipping idols.

Among the proofs of revelation is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Do you worship what you carve?﴾ [al-Saffat: 95] ﴿While God created you and what you do?﴾ [al-Saffat: 96], and others besides. Mentioning that it is a prohibition by revelation does not indicate that it was not also forbidden by the proofs of reason. When he was forbidden to worship idols, he informed them that he had been commanded to submit to God, Exalted is He. Then he clarified the matter of unity (wahdaniyya) and divinity (uluhiyya), of which their idols are devoid in any respect, by considering the stages of the son of Adam's creation, beginning with his first origin, which is dust.

Then he pointed to procreation by His creating him from a drop of semen. "Child" (tifl) is a collective noun (ism jins), or the meaning is: "then He brings you forth," i.e., each one of you as a child. The discussion of reaching full strength (bulugh al-ashudd) has already been presented.

As for "min qabl" (before that), Mujahid said: "before one becomes an old man." It has been said that it may also mean before these states, when one comes forth as a miscarriage. It has also been said that it is an expression of his being subject to the stages mentioned, and it is not restricted to what precedes old age; rather, some of them die before being brought forth as infants, another before reaching full strength, and another before old age.

﴿And that you may reach﴾ is connected to an elided element, meaning: He keeps you alive so that you may reach, i.e., so that each one of you may reach an appointed term that he does not exceed. Mujahid said: "It refers to the death of all." It has been said that it is the Day of Resurrection. As for "perhaps you will understand," it refers to the lesson and proofs contained in this, if you reflect upon it and ponder it.

When He mentioned the stages of existence, He mentioned that He is the One characterized by giving life and causing death, and that whenever His will becomes related to the bringing into existence of a thing, He brings it into existence without delay. The discussion of similar sentences has already been presented.

Then, after these signs became manifest, He said: Do you not marvel at those who dispute the mission of the Messenger, peace be upon him, and the Book that he brought? This is shown by His saying: ﴿those who denied the Book and what We sent with Our messengers﴾. Then He threatened them with His saying: ﴿They will come to know﴾. This is the view of the majority.

Muhammad ibn Sirin and others said: it is an allusion to the people of desires (ahl al-ahwa') from among the community. They related a hadith to this effect and said: it refers to the people of qadar (divine decree and human will) and those who follow their path. It follows for those who hold this view that His saying ﴿those who denied﴾ be taken as a new independent statement about the disbelievers, with ﴿those who denied﴾ as the subject and ﴿They will come to know﴾ as its predicate. As for the apparent reading, ﴿those who﴾ is a substitute (badal) for the preceding ﴿those who﴾, or the predicate of an elided subject, or in the accusative by way of censure. And "idh" (when) is an adverb of time referring to the past, so the future verb does not govern it, just as one does not say "sa-aqumu amsi" (I will stand yesterday). It has been said that "idh" here takes the place of "idha" (whenever), and that its position is metaphorical; so "idh" here means "idha," and the certainty of the event's occurrence justified this, and it was expressed in the past tense even though the meaning is future.

Al-Nakha'i said: If one shackle of the shackles of Hell were placed upon a mountain, it would drag it until it reached the black water.

He recited ﴿wa-l-salasilu﴾ (and the chains) as a coordination with ﴿al-aghlal﴾ (the shackles), with ﴿yus'habun﴾ (they are dragged) in the passive voice.

It will be said to them: "Where are the idols that you used to worship in the world?" They will say: ﴿They have strayed from us﴾, i.e., they have been lost to us, vanished, and disappeared. Then their statements become confused, and they resort to lying, saying: ﴿Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before.﴾ This is among the greatest confusion of mind and reasoning.

When it became clear to them that they had been nothing, and that their worship of them had achieved nothing, just as you say: "I thought that so-and-so was something, but when you test him he is nothing, so you find no reward from him."

Their saying ﴿They have strayed from us﴾, together with His saying ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell; you will be coming to it﴾ [al-Anbiya': 98], may be understood to mean that this occurs during their rebuke, so the idols were not with them at that time; or, when they did not benefit them, they said ﴿They have strayed from us﴾, even if they were with them.

﴿Thus﴾ means: like this quality and in this order, ﴿God leads astray the disbelievers.﴾ Al-Zamakhshari said: i.e., like the straying of their gods from them; He leads them astray from their gods, so that even if they sought the gods, or the gods sought them, they would not meet.

That leading astray is because of what you used to have of exultation and insolence, ﴿without right﴾, which is polytheism and worship of idols.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: That punishment in which you are is because of what you used to exult in on earth through sins and disbelief. The end.

As for ﴿tamrahun﴾ (you are insolent), Ibn 'Abbas said: it is boasting and arrogance; Mujahid said: it is pride and frivolity. The end. He said this to them as rebuke, meaning: this is because of what you used to display in the world of joy in sins and abundance of wealth, followers, and health.

Al-Dahhak said: "al-farah" is joy and delight, and "al-maraḥ" is transgression. In a hadith: "God hates the exulting, arrogant ones, and loves every grieving heart."

Or, after entering it, they are commanded to enter the seven gates, for each gate has a specified portion of the disbelievers; this command to enter thus implies division into each gate.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Enter﴾ means: it is said to them before this dialogue, at the beginning of the matter: "Enter," because this address is only after they have entered, and at the time when the shackles are on their necks.

The gates of Hell are the seven leading to its layers and its seven levels. The end.

﴿Abiding﴾ is a circumstantial clause of anticipated state (hal muqaddara), and it indicates lasting dwelling. Thus the construction comes: ﴿How evil is the abode of the arrogant﴾; the meaning is: how evil is the entrance of the arrogant, because entry itself does not last, so he did not exaggerate in condemning it, unlike lasting dwelling.

When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ ﴿Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of God? How are they turned away?﴾ ﴿Those who denied the Book and what We sent with Our messengers. They will come to know.﴾ ﴿When the shackles are around their necks and the chains, they are dragged,﴾ ﴿into the boiling water, then in the Fire they are kindled.﴾ ﴿Then it is said to them, "Where are those you used to associate with God?"﴾ ﴿They say, "They have strayed from us. Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before." Thus God leads astray the disbelievers.﴾ ﴿That is because you used to exult in the land without right, and because you used to be insolent.﴾ ﴿Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein. How evil is the abode of the arrogant.﴾

God commanded His Prophet, peace be upon him, to inform them that he had been forbidden to worship their idols when the clear proofs had come to him from his Lord. This is a prohibition by revelation (sam'), although it is also forbidden by the proofs of reason ('aql). The proofs of revelation and the proofs of reason thus converge on the prohibition of worshipping idols.

Among the proofs of revelation is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Do you worship what you carve?﴾ [al-Saffat: 95] ﴿While God created you and what you do?﴾ [al-Saffat: 96], and others besides. Mentioning that it is a prohibition by revelation does not indicate that it was not also forbidden by the proofs of reason. When he was forbidden to worship idols, he informed them that he had been commanded to submit to God, Exalted is He. Then he clarified the matter of unity (wahdaniyya) and divinity (uluhiyya), of which their idols are devoid in any respect, by considering the stages of the son of Adam's creation, beginning with his first origin, which is dust.

Then he pointed to procreation by His creating him from a drop of semen. "Child" (tifl) is a collective noun (ism jins), or the meaning is: "then He brings you forth," i.e., each one of you as a child. The discussion of reaching full strength (bulugh al-ashudd) has already been presented.

As for "min qabl" (before that), Mujahid said: "before one becomes an old man." It has been said that it may also mean before these states, when one comes forth as a miscarriage. It has also been said that it is an expression of his being subject to the stages mentioned, and it is not restricted to what precedes old age; rather, some of them die before being brought forth as infants, another before reaching full strength, and another before old age.

﴿And that you may reach﴾ is connected to an elided element, meaning: He keeps you alive so that you may reach, i.e., so that each one of you may reach an appointed term that he does not exceed. Mujahid said: "It refers to the death of all." It has been said that it is the Day of Resurrection. As for "perhaps you will understand," it refers to the lesson and proofs contained in this, if you reflect upon it and ponder it.

When He mentioned the stages of existence, He mentioned that He is the One characterized by giving life and causing death, and that whenever His will becomes related to the bringing into existence of a thing, He brings it into existence without delay. The discussion of similar sentences has already been presented.

Then, after these signs became manifest, He said: Do you not marvel at those who dispute the mission of the Messenger, peace be upon him, and the Book that he brought? This is shown by His saying: ﴿those who denied the Book and what We sent with Our messengers﴾. Then He threatened them with His saying: ﴿They will come to know﴾. This is the view of the majority.

Muhammad ibn Sirin and others said: it is an allusion to the people of desires (ahl al-ahwa') from among the community. They related a hadith to this effect and said: it refers to the people of qadar (divine decree and human will) and those who follow their path. It follows for those who hold this view that His saying ﴿those who denied﴾ be taken as a new independent statement about the disbelievers, with ﴿those who denied﴾ as the subject and ﴿They will come to know﴾ as its predicate. As for the apparent reading, ﴿those who﴾ is a substitute (badal) for the preceding ﴿those who﴾, or the predicate of an elided subject, or in the accusative by way of censure. And "idh" (when) is an adverb of time referring to the past, so the future verb does not govern it, just as one does not say "sa-aqumu amsi" (I will stand yesterday). It has been said that "idh" here takes the place of "idha" (whenever), and that its position is metaphorical; so "idh" here means "idha," and the certainty of the event's occurrence justified this, and it was expressed in the past tense even though the meaning is future.

Al-Nakha'i said: If one shackle of the shackles of Hell were placed upon a mountain, it would drag it until it reached the black water.

He recited ﴿wa-l-salasilu﴾ (and the chains) as a coordination with ﴿al-aghlal﴾ (the shackles), with ﴿yus'habun﴾ (they are dragged) in the passive voice.

Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Zayd ibn 'Ali, Ibn Wathhab, and al-Musi' in his choice of reading recited (p-475) ﴿wa-l-salasila﴾ with the accusative as the object, and ﴿yus'habun﴾ in the active voice. This is the coordination of a verbal sentence upon a nominal sentence.

A group, including Ibn 'Abbas, recited (wa-l-salasili) with the lam in the genitive. Ibn 'Atiyya said: this is by way of an assumed construction, "when their necks are in the shackles and the chains," so it coordinates upon the intended meaning of the speech and not upon the arrangement of the wording, since its arrangement in that case is inverted. This is in the manner of the Arabs' saying: "I put the qalansuwa (cap) on my head," and in the codex of Ubayy: (and in the chains they are dragged).

Al-Zamakhshari said: The reasoning is that if one were to say, "when their necks are in the shackles," in place of His saying ﴿when the shackles are around their necks﴾, it would be correct and sound. Since the two expressions are interchangeable, His saying ﴿wa-l-salasilu﴾ is taken as referring to the other expression. A similar example is the saying of the poet:

Ill-omened ones, they do not reform a tribe, nor a crier except with the separation of its crow.

It is as if it were said: "with those who reform." And it was recited (wa-bi-l-salasili). The end of his words. This is called "coordination upon an assumed construction" ('atf 'ala al-tawahhum). But the assumption of inserting a prepositional particle before "muslihin" is closer than altering the entire structure of the sentence, while the recitation alters the entire structure of the preceding sentence. A similar example is the saying of the poet:

Are you truly going to see, by the Thu'aylibat (a place), nor a desert (baydaa') bearing a swift camel that carries?
Nor one who overtakes while the night is young, with a loaded camel, among the rugged parts of the valley.

The assumed construction is: "you are not innocent, nor one who overtakes."

What Ibn 'Atiyya and al-Zamakhshari said was preceded by al-Farra', who said: Whoever puts "salasil" in the genitive has taken it according to the meaning, because the meaning is: their necks are in the shackles and the chains.

Al-Zajjaj said: Whoever reads "wa-l-salasili" with the genitive, the meaning according to him is: "and in the chains they are dragged."

Ibn al-Anbari said: The genitive on this meaning is not permissible. If you say, "Zayd is in the house," it is not good to omit the preposition and say "Zayd the house." Then he mentioned al-Farra's interpretation, and explained the recitation, and then said: as you say, "'Abd Allah contended with Zayd, the two wise ones (al-'aqilayn)," with the accusative and nominative of al-'aqilayn, because when one of them contends with his companion, the other has contended with him. The end.

This matter is not permissible according to the Basran grammarians, and its permissibility is reported from Muhammad ibn Sa'fan al-Kufi, who said: because each of the two is both agent and object. And it is recited: (wa-bi-l-salasili yus'habun). Perhaps this recitation led al-Zajjaj to interpret the genitive as implying an elided preposition, which is an anomalous interpretation.

When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ ﴿Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of God? How are they turned away?﴾ ﴿Those who denied the Book and what We sent with Our messengers. They will come to know.﴾ ﴿When the shackles are around their necks and the chains, they are dragged,﴾ ﴿into the boiling water, then in the Fire they are kindled.﴾ ﴿Then it is said to them, "Where are those you used to associate with God?"﴾ ﴿They say, "They have strayed from us. Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before." Thus God leads astray the disbelievers.﴾ ﴿That is because you used to exult in the land without right, and because you used to be insolent.﴾ ﴿Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein. How evil is the abode of the arrogant.﴾

This is a prohibition by revelation (sam'), although it is also forbidden by the proofs of reason ('aql). The proofs of revelation and the proofs of reason thus converge on the prohibition of worshipping idols.

Mentioning that it is a prohibition by revelation does not indicate that it was not also forbidden by the proofs of reason. When he was forbidden to worship idols, he informed them that he had been commanded to submit to God, Exalted is He. Then he clarified the matter of unity (wahdaniyya) and divinity (uluhiyya), of which their idols are devoid in any respect, by considering the stages of the son of Adam's creation, beginning with his first origin, which is dust.

Then he pointed to procreation by His creating him from a drop of semen. "Child" (tifl) is a collective noun (ism jins), or the meaning is: "then He brings you forth," i.e., each one of you as a child. The discussion of reaching full strength (bulugh al-ashudd) has already been presented.

As for "min qabl" (before that), Mujahid said: "before one becomes an old man." It has been said that it may also mean before these states, when one comes forth as a miscarriage. It has also been said that it is an expression of his being subject to the stages mentioned, and it is not restricted to what precedes old age; rather, some of them die before being brought forth as infants, another before reaching full strength, and another before old age.

﴿And that you may reach﴾ is connected to an elided element, meaning: He keeps you alive so that you may reach, i.e., so that each one of you may reach an appointed term that he does not exceed. Mujahid said: "It refers to the death of all." It has been said that it is the Day of Resurrection. As for "perhaps you will understand," it refers to the lesson and proofs contained in this, if you reflect upon it and ponder it.

When He mentioned the stages of existence, He mentioned that He is the One characterized by giving life and causing death, and that whenever His will becomes related to the bringing into existence of a thing, He brings it into existence without delay. The discussion of similar sentences has already been presented.

Then, after these signs became manifest, He said: Do you not marvel at those who dispute the mission of the Messenger, peace be upon him, and the Book that he brought? This is shown by His saying: ﴿those who denied the Book and what We sent with Our messengers﴾. Then He threatened them with His saying: ﴿They will come to know﴾. This is the view of the majority.

Muhammad ibn Sirin and others said: it is an allusion to the people of desires (ahl al-ahwa') from among the community. They related a hadith to this effect and said: it refers to the people of qadar (divine decree and human will) and those who follow their path. It follows for those who hold this view that His saying ﴿those who denied﴾ be taken as a new independent statement about the disbelievers, with ﴿those who denied﴾ as the subject and ﴿They will come to know﴾ as its predicate. As for the apparent reading, ﴿those who﴾ is a substitute (badal) for the preceding ﴿those who﴾, or the predicate of an elided subject, or in the accusative by way of censure. And "idh" (when) is an adverb of time referring to the past, so the future verb does not govern it, just as one does not say "sa-aqumu amsi" (I will stand yesterday). It has been said that "idh" here takes the place of "idha" (whenever), and that its position is metaphorical; so "idh" here means "idha," and the certainty of the event's occurrence justified this, and it was expressed in the past tense even though the meaning is future.

Al-Nakha'i said: If one shackle of the shackles of Hell were placed upon a mountain, it would drag it until it reached the black water.

He recited ﴿wa-l-salasilu﴾ (and the chains) as a coordination with ﴿al-aghlal﴾ (the shackles), with ﴿yus'habun﴾ (they are dragged) in the passive voice.

Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Zayd ibn 'Ali, Ibn Wathhab, and al-Musi' in his choice of reading recited (p-475) ﴿wa-l-salasila﴾ with the accusative as the object, and ﴿yus'habun﴾ in the active voice. This is the coordination of a verbal sentence upon a nominal sentence.

A group, including Ibn 'Abbas, recited (wa-l-salasili) with the lam in the genitive. Ibn 'Atiyya said: this is by way of an assumed construction, "when their necks are in the shackles and the chains," so it coordinates upon the intended meaning of the speech and not upon the arrangement of the wording, since its arrangement in that case is inverted. This is in the manner of the Arabs' saying: "I put the qalansuwa (cap) on my head," and in the codex of Ubayy: (and in the chains they are dragged).

Al-Zamakhshari said: The reasoning is that if one were to say, "when their necks are in the shackles," in place of His saying ﴿when the shackles are around their necks﴾, it would be correct and sound. Since the two expressions are interchangeable, His saying ﴿wa-l-salasilu﴾ is taken as referring to the other expression. A similar example is the saying of the poet:

Ill-omened ones, they do not reform a tribe, nor a crier except with the separation of its crow.

It is as if it were said: "with those who reform." And it was recited (wa-bi-l-salasili). The end of his words. This is called "coordination upon an assumed construction" ('atf 'ala al-tawahhum). But the assumption of inserting a prepositional particle before "muslihin" is closer than altering the entire structure of the sentence, while the recitation alters the entire structure of the preceding sentence. A similar example is the saying of the poet:

Are you truly going to see, by the Thu'aylibat (a place), nor a desert (baydaa') bearing a swift camel that carries?
Nor one who overtakes while the night is young, with a loaded camel, among the rugged parts of the valley.

The assumed construction is: "you are not innocent, nor one who overtakes."

What Ibn 'Atiyya and al-Zamakhshari said was preceded by al-Farra', who said: Whoever puts "salasil" in the genitive has taken it according to the meaning, because the meaning is: their necks are in the shackles and the chains.

Al-Zajjaj said: Whoever reads "wa-l-salasili" with the genitive, the meaning according to him is: "and in the chains they are dragged."

Ibn al-Anbari said: The genitive on this meaning is not permissible. If you say, "Zayd is in the house," it is not good to omit the preposition and say "Zayd the house." Then he mentioned al-Farra's interpretation, and explained the recitation, and then said: as you say, "'Abd Allah contended with Zayd, the two wise ones (al-'aqilayn)," with the accusative and nominative of al-'aqilayn, because when one of them contends with his companion, the other has contended with him. The end.

This matter is not permissible according to the Basran grammarians, and its permissibility is reported from Muhammad ibn Sa'fan al-Kufi, who said: because each of the two is both agent and object. And it is recited: (wa-bi-l-salasili yus'habun). Perhaps this recitation led al-Zajjaj to interpret the genitive as implying an elided preposition, which is an anomalous interpretation.

Ibn 'Abbas said, regarding the reading of the one who put ﴿wa-l-salasila﴾ in the accusative and opened the ya' of (yas'habun): if they drag them, it is harder for them; they are burdened with this while unable to bear it.

Mujahid said: ﴿yusjarun﴾ (they are kindled) means: they are thrown into it, and so they become fuel for it. Al-Suddi said: ﴿yusjarun﴾ means they are burned.

Then God, Exalted is He, informed that they will be made to stand on the Day of Resurrection for rebuke and reproach. It will be said to them: "Where are the idols that you used to worship in the world?" They will say: ﴿They have strayed from us﴾, i.e., they have been lost to us, vanished, and disappeared. Then their statements become confused, and they resort to lying, saying: ﴿Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before.﴾ This is among the greatest confusion of mind and reasoning.

When it became clear to them that they had been nothing, and that their worship of them had achieved nothing, just as you say: "I thought that so-and-so was something, but when you test him he is nothing, so you find no reward from him."

Their saying ﴿They have strayed from us﴾, together with His saying ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell; you will be coming to it﴾ [al-Anbiya': 98], may be understood to mean that this occurs during their rebuke, so the idols were not with them at that time; or, when they did not benefit them, they said ﴿They have strayed from us﴾, even if they were with them.

﴿Thus﴾ means: like this quality and in this order, ﴿God leads astray the disbelievers.﴾ Al-Zamakhshari said: i.e., like the straying of their gods from them; He leads them astray from their gods, so that even if they sought the gods, or the gods sought them, they would not meet.

That leading astray is because of what you used to have of exultation and insolence, ﴿without right﴾, which is polytheism and worship of idols.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: That punishment in which you are is because of what you used to exult in on earth through sins and disbelief. The end.

As for ﴿tamrahun﴾ (you are insolent), Ibn 'Abbas said: it is boasting and arrogance; Mujahid said: it is pride and frivolity. The end. He said this to them as rebuke, meaning: this is because of what you used to display in the world of joy in sins and abundance of wealth, followers, and health.

Al-Dahhak said: "al-farah" is joy and delight, and "al-maraḥ" is transgression. In a hadith: "God hates the exulting, arrogant ones, and loves every grieving heart."
